<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of November&#160;16,&#160;2017, 29,984,434 shares of the Registrant&#8217;s common stock were outstanding.  The aggregate market value of shares of common stock held by non-affiliates as of March&#160;31,&#160;2017, was $2,562,036,264 (based upon the closing sales price of $86.05 per share).</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Documents Incorporated by Reference </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Part III incorporates information by reference to the registrant&#8217;s definitive proxy statement, to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission within 120 days after the close of the fiscal year ended September&#160;29, 2017. </p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU3"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">PART I</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">This Report includes a number of forward-looking statements that reflect the Company&#8217;s current views with respect to future events and financial performance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Please refer to the section addressing forward-looking information on page&#160;10 for further discussion.&nbsp;&nbsp;In this report, &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our,&#8221; &#8220;us,&#8221; &#8220;Company,&#8221; and &#8220;Esterline&#8221; refer to Esterline Technologies Corporation and subsidiaries, unless otherwise noted or context otherwise indicates. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Explanatory Note</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We changed our fiscal year to the twelve months ending the last Friday in September, effective beginning with the year ended on September&#160;30, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, our 2015 fiscal year was shortened from twelve months to an eleven-month transition period ended on October&#160;2, 2015.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Unless otherwise noted in this Part I: </p>
<div align="left">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.42%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">When financial results for fiscal 2016 are compared to the prior-year period, the results compare the twelve-month periods ended September&#160;30, 2016, and October&#160;2, 2015, respectively.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The results for the twelve-month period ended October&#160;2, 2015, are unaudited.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Item&#160;1.&#160;&#160;Business </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">General Development of Business</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Esterline, a Delaware corporation formed in 1967, is a leading specialized manufacturing company principally serving aerospace and defense customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We design, manufacture and market highly engineered products and systems for application within the industries we serve.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our current business and strategic plan focuses on continued development of our products principally for aerospace and defense markets in three key technology segments:&nbsp;&nbsp;Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls, Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems, and Advanced Materials.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our products are often mission critical, which have been designed into particular military and commercial platforms, and in certain cases can only be replaced by products of other manufacturers following a formal certification process.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are concentrating our efforts to expand our capabilities in these markets, anticipate the global needs of our customers and respond to such needs with comprehensive solutions.&nbsp;&nbsp;These efforts focus on continuous research and new product development, acquisitions, and strategic realignment of operations to expand our capabilities as a more comprehensive supplier to our customers across our entire product offering.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such expansion included the January 2015 acquisition of the defense, aerospace and training display business, Esterline Advanced Displays (EAD), of Belgium-based Barco N.V. (Barco).&nbsp;&nbsp;This acquisition is described in more detail in the &#8220;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#8221; section of Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Continuing Operations contained in Item&#160;7 of this report.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In December 2013 we announced the acceleration of our plans to consolidate certain facilities and create cost efficiencies through shared services in sales, general and administrative and support functions, which were completed in fiscal 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;We incurred costs of $8.7&#160;million in fiscal 2016 and $14.6&#160;million in the recast twelve-month period of fiscal 2015 associated with these activities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The costs include severance, relocation of facilities, and losses from the write off of certain property, plant and equipment.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In March 2014 we entered into a Consent Agreement with the U.S. Department of State&#8217;s Directorate of Defense Trade Controls Office of Defense Trade Controls Compliance (DTCC) to resolve alleged International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) civil violations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among other things, the Consent Agreement required us to pay a $20&#160;million penalty, of which $10&#160;million was suspended and eligible for offset credit.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2016 the DTCC approved costs we incurred to implement compliance measures to fully offset the $10&#160;million suspended payment.&nbsp;&nbsp;<font style="color:#000000;">On September&#160;5, 2017, the DTCC notified us that it is closing the Consent Agreement.&#160;The closing of the Consent Agreement was based on our certifications that all aspects of the Consent Agreement have been implemented and that our trade compliance program is adequate to identify, prevent, detect, correct, and report violations of the Arms Export Control Act (AECA) and ITAR, as well as the DTCC&#8217;s assessment that we have fulfilled the terms of the Consent Agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In fiscal 2014 our Board of Directors approved the plan to sell certain non-core business units including Eclipse Electronic Systems, Inc. (Eclipse), a manufacturer of embedded communication intercept receivers for signal intelligence applications; Wallop Defence Systems, Ltd. (Wallop), a manufacturer of flare countermeasure devices; a small distribution business; Pacific Aerospace and Electronics Inc. (PA&amp;E), a manufacturer of hermetically sealed electrical connectors; and a small manufacturing business.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of September 30, 2017, we have sold these business units except for the land and building at Eclipse and Wallop, which are currently held for sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;These businesses are reported as discontinued operations.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU4"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We recorded a loss from discontinued operations of $7.3&#160;million, $15.3&#160;million, and $40.3&#160;million in fiscal 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our products have a long history in the aerospace and defense industry and are found on most military and commercial aircraft, helicopters, and land-based systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, our products are used on the majority of active and in-production U.S. military aircraft and on every Boeing commercial aircraft platform manufactured in the past 75 years.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, our products are supplied to Airbus, many of the major regional and business jet manufacturers, and the major aircraft engine manufacturers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We work closely with OEMs on new, highly engineered products with the objective of such products becoming designed into our customers&#8217; platforms; this integration often results in sole-source positions for OEM production and aftermarket business.&nbsp;&nbsp;We broadly categorize our commercial and military aerospace aftermarket sales as retrofit, repair services, and spare parts.&nbsp;&nbsp;Spare parts alone made up approximately 9% of total sales in fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Retrofit and repair services, which represent 3% of total sales in fiscal 2017, carry higher margins than OEM sales but lower margins than spare parts sales.&nbsp;&nbsp;In many cases, our aftermarket sales span the entire life of an aircraft. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We differentiate ourselves through our engineering and manufacturing capabilities and our reputation for safety, quality, on-time delivery, reliability, and innovation &#8211; all embodied in the Esterline Operating System, our way of approaching business that helps ensure all employees are focused on continuous improvement, teamwork, a safe work environment and compliance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Safety of our operations is a critical factor in our business, and accordingly, we incorporate applicable regulatory guidance in the design of our facilities and train our employees using a behavior-based approach that focuses on safety-designed work habits and on-going safety audits.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our industries are highly regulated, and compliance with applicable regulations, including export control and anti-bribery regulations, is an important focus in our business.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have a global code of business conduct and ethics, and we provide corporate-wide training and maintain local ethics advisors and export control specialists in our business units to support our compliance efforts.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017 we continued our significant efforts to build and strengthen our trade compliance program, driven in large part by the requirements of the Consent Agreement discussed above.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our sales are diversified across three broad markets:&nbsp;&nbsp;defense, commercial aerospace and general industrial.&nbsp;&nbsp;For fiscal 2017, approximately 30% of our sales were from the defense market, 40% from the commercial aerospace market, and 30% from the general industrial market.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financial Information About Industry Segments</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A summary of net sales to unaffiliated customers, operating earnings and identifiable assets attributable to our business segments for fiscal 2017, 2016, and 2015 is reported in Note&#160;18 to the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Financial Statements under Item&#160;8 of this report.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Description of Business</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls business segment includes avionics systems, control and communication systems, and interface technologies capabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Avionics systems designs, develops and integrates cockpit avionics solutions as well as providing visualization solutions for commercial and defense applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;Control and communication systems designs and manufactures technology interface solutions for military and commercial aircraft and land- and sea-based military vehicles.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interface technologies manufactures and develops custom control panels and input systems for medical, industrial, military and gaming industries.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are a market leader in global positioning systems (GPS), head-up displays, enhanced vision systems, flight management systems, touchscreen display solutions and secure communication systems, all of which are used in a broad variety of applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we develop, manufacture and market sophisticated, highly reliable component systems including lighted push-button and rotary switches, keyboards, lighted indicators, panels and displays.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our products have been integrated into many existing aircraft designs, including every Boeing commercial aircraft platform currently in production.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are a Tier&#160;1 supplier on the Boeing 787 and 777X programs to design and manufacture all of the cockpit overhead panels and embedded software for these systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;<font style="color:#000000;">We provide high-quality and affordable visual display solutions to the air traffic control, naval, ground vehicles and unmanned systems and simulation and training markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our simulation and training solutions include a 360-degree rear projection display that offers high contrast and resolution and various types of large field-of-view collimated displays, and a deployable display with a roll-up, seamless spherical screen</font><font style="color:#000000;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>We manufacture control sticks, grips and wheels, as well as specialized switching systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;In this area we primarily serve commercial and military aviation and airborne and ground-based military equipment manufacturing customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, we are a leading manufacturer of pilot control grips for most types of military fighter jets and helicopters.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, our software engineering center supports our customers&#8217; needs with applications such as flight management systems, air data computers and engine control systems.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">4</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU5"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our proprietary products meet critical operational requirements and provide customers with significant technological advantages in areas such as night vision compatibility and active-matrix liquid-crystal displays (a technology enabling pilots to rea</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">d display screens in a variety of light conditions as well as from extreme angles).&nbsp;&nbsp;Our products are incorporated in a wide variety of platforms ranging from military helicopters, fighters and transports, to commercial wide- and narrow-body, regional and </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">business jets.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017 some of our largest customers for these products included Airbus, BAE Systems, The Boeing Company, Bombardier, FAA, Honeywell, L3 Technologies, Leonardo, Lockheed Martin, Pilatus, Rockwell Collins, Textron, Thales, and Triman</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition, we design and manufacture ruggedized military personal communication equipment, primarily headsets, handsets and field communications.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are the sole supplier of Active Noise Reduction (ANR) headsets to the British Army&#8217;s tracked and wheeled vehicle fleets under the Bowman communication system program.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also supply ANR headsets to the U.S. Army&#8217;s tracked and wheeled vehicle fleets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, we are the primary ANR headset supplier to the Canadian Army and have a long-standing relationship with allied armies around the world.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017 some of our largest customers for these products included BAE Systems, The Boeing Company, NATO Supply Procurement Agency, the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD), and Simex Defence.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We also manufacture a full line of keyboard, switch and input technologies for specialized medical equipment, high-tech gaming applications, and communication systems for military applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;These products include custom keyboards, keypads, and input devices that integrate cursor control devices, barcode scanners, displays, video, and voice activation and touch screens.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also produce instruments that are used for point-of-use and point-of-care diagnostics.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have developed a wide variety of technologies, including plastic and vinyl membranes that protect high-use switches and fully depressible buttons, and backlit elastomer switch coverings that are resistant to exposure from harsh chemicals.&nbsp;&nbsp;These technologies now serve as the foundation for a small but growing portion of our product line.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017, some of our largest customers for these products included Aristocrat Technologies, General Electric, Nuance, Philips, and Stat-Diagnostic.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems business segment includes power systems, connection technologies and advanced sensors capabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;We develop and manufacture high-precision temperature, pressure and speed sensors principally for aerospace customers, electrical interconnect systems for severe environments for aerospace, defense, geophysics&#160;&amp; marine, rail, and nuclear customers, as well as electrical power switching, control and data communication devices, and other related systems principally for aerospace and defense customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are the sole-source and aftersales supplier of temperature probes for use on all versions of the General Electric/Snecma CFM-56 jet engine.&nbsp;&nbsp;The CFM-56 jet engine has an installed base of over 30,000, and is standard equipment on the current generation Boeing 737 aircraft and approximately 60% of Airbus aircraft.&nbsp;&nbsp;We manufacture sensors for the environmental control system for Boeing 787 aircraft, and provide the primary power distribution assembly for the Airbus A400M military transport.&nbsp;&nbsp;We will provide the primary power distribution assembly for Embraer E-2 and Mitsubishi Regional Jet.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, we have a Tier&#160;1 position with Rolls-Royce for a large suite of sensors for the engines that power the A400M and A350.&nbsp;&nbsp;We design and manufacture interconnect solutions for harsh environments, connectors, backshells, conduits, planet probe interconnectors, and launcher umbilicals.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also design and manufacture composite connectors for the Boeing 787.&nbsp;&nbsp;The principal customers for our products in this business segment are jet engine manufacturers, airframe and industrial manufacturers.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017 some of our largest customers for these products included Airbus, BJG, The Boeing Company, Bombardier, Flame, General Electric, Rolls-Royce, Safran, TTI, Inc., and United Technologies Corporation (UTC) Aerospace Systems.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Advanced Materials</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Advanced Materials business segment includes engineered materials and defense technologies capabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;We develop and manufacture high-performance elastomer products used in a wide range of commercial aerospace, space and military applications, and highly engineered thermal components for commercial aerospace and industrial applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also develop and manufacture combustible ordnance and countermeasures for military applications.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Specialized High-Performance Applications<font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;We specialize in the development of proprietary formulations for silicone rubber and other elastomer products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our elastomer products are engineered to address specific customer requirements where superior performance in high temperature, high pressure, caustic, abrasive and other difficult environments is critical.&nbsp;&nbsp;These products include clamping devices, thermal fire barrier insulation products, sealing systems, tubing and coverings designed in custom-molded shapes.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of the products include proprietary elastomers that are specifically designed for use on or near a jet engine.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are a leading U.S. supplier of high-performance elastomer products to the aerospace industry, with our primary customers for these products being jet and rocket engine manufacturers, commercial and military airframe manufacturers, as well as commercial airlines.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017 some of the largest customers for these products included The Boeing Company, KLX Aerospace Solutions, Lockheed Martin, and Northrup Grumman.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">5</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU6"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We also develop and manufacture high temperature, lightweight metallic insulation systems for aerospace and marine applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our commercial aerospace programs include the Boeing 737, Airbus A320 and A380 series aircraft, and the Interna</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">tional Aero Engines V2500 and Rolls-Royce BR710 engines.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our insulation material is used on diesel engine manifolds for earthmoving and agricultural applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we specialize in the development of thermal protection for fire, nuclear, and </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">petro-chemical industries.&nbsp;&nbsp;We design and manufacture high temperature components for industrial and marine markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our manufacturing processes consist of cutting, pressing, and welding stainless steel, inconel, and titanium fabrications.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> some of the largest customers of these products included Airbus, Rolls-Royce, and Spirit AeroSystems.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Ordnance and Countermeasure Applications<font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;We develop and manufacture combustible ordnance and warfare countermeasure devices for military customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We manufacture molded fiber cartridge cases, mortar increments, igniter tubes and other combustible ordnance components primarily for the DoD.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are currently the sole supplier of combustible casings utilized by the U.S. Armed Forces.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sales are made either directly to the DoD or through prime contractors and General Dynamics.&nbsp;&nbsp;These products include the combustible case for the U.S. Army&#8217;s new generation 155mm Modular Artillery Charge System, the 120mm combustible case used with the main armament system on the U.S. Army and Marine Corps&#8217; M1-A1/2 tanks, and the 60mm, 81mm and 120mm combustible mortar increments.&nbsp;&nbsp;We were recently selected as the exclusive provider of high- and low-velocity payloads for 40mm infrared training rounds.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are one of two suppliers to the U.S. Army of infrared decoy flares used by aircraft to help protect against radar and infrared guided missiles.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are currently the only supplier to the U.S. Army of countermeasures against radar-based threats.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017, in addition to the DoD, some of the largest customers of these products included Orbital ATK, General Dynamics, and Rikei.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A summary of product lines contributing sales of 10% or more of total sales for fiscal 2017, 2016, and 2015 is reported in Note&#160;18 to the Consolidated Financial Statements under Item&#160;8 of this report.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Marketing and Distribution</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We believe that a key to continued success is our ability to meet customer requirements both domestically and internationally.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have and will continue to improve our world-wide sales and distribution channels in order to provide wider market coverage and to improve the effectiveness of our customers&#8217; supply chain.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, our medical device assembly operation in Shanghai, China, serves our global medical customers, our service center in Singapore improves our capabilities in Asia for our temperature sensor customers, and our engineering and marketing offices in Bangalore, India, facilitate marketing opportunities in India.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other enhancements include combining sales and marketing forces of our operating units where appropriate, cross-training our sales representatives on multiple product lines, and cross-stocking our spares and components.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the technical and highly engineered product segments in which we compete, relationship selling is particularly important in targeted marketing segments where customer and supplier design and engineering inputs need to be tightly integrated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Participation in industry trade shows is an effective method of meeting customers, introducing new products, and exchanging technical specifications.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to technical and industry conferences, our products are supported through direct internal international sales efforts, as well as through manufacturer representatives and selected distributors.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of September&#160;29, 2017, 364 sales people, 253 representatives, and 315 distributors supported our operations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Backlog</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Backlog was $1.3&#160;billion at September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;We estimate that approximately $440&#160;million of backlog is scheduled to be shipped after fiscal 2018.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Backlog is subject to cancellation until delivered, and therefore, we cannot assure that our backlog will be converted into revenue in any particular period or at all.&nbsp;&nbsp;Except for the released portion, backlog also does not include fixed-price, multi-year contracts.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Competition</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU7"></a>Our products and services are affected by varying degrees of competition.&nbsp;&nbsp;We compete with other companies in most markets we serve.&nbsp;&nbsp;Many of these companies have far greater sales volumes and financial resources than we do.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of our competitors are also our customers or suppliers on certain programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The principal competitive factors in the commercial markets in which we participate are customer intimacy, product performance, on-time delivery performance, quality, service and price.&nbsp;&nbsp;Part of product performance requires expenditures in research and development that lead to product improvement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The market for many of our products may be affected by rapid and significant technological changes and new product introductions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our principal competitors include Astronautics, BAE, Bose, Eaton, Elbit, EMS, Essex Industries, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, IAI, L-3, Otto Controls, RAFI, Rockwell Collins, SELEX, Telephonics, Thales, Ultra Electronics, Universal Avionics Systems Corporation, and Zodiac in our Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls segment; Ametek, Amphenol, Eaton, Meggitt, STPI-Deutsch, TE Connectivity, Woodward and Zodiac in our Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems segment; and Alloy Surfaces, AMTEC, Chemring, Doncasters, Hi-Temp, J&amp;M, JPR Hutchinson, Kmass, </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">6</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Meggitt (including Dunlop Standard Aerospace Group), Rheinmetall, Trelleborg, ULVA, UTC Aerospace </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Systems, UMPCO, and Woodward Products in our Advanced Materials segment.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Research and Development</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our product development and design programs utilize an extensive base of professional engineers, technicians and support personnel, supplemented by outside engineering and consulting firms when needed.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017 we expended $103.0&#160;million for research, development and engineering, compared with $95.9&#160;million in fiscal 2016 and $100.4&#160;million in the recast twelve-month period of fiscal 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;Research and development expense has averaged 5.0% of sales per year for the three years ended September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe continued product development is key to our long-term growth, and consequently, we consistently invest in research and development.&nbsp;&nbsp;Examples include research and development projects relating to avionics displays, power systems, and controls.&nbsp;&nbsp;We actively participate in customer-funded research and development programs.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreign Operations</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our foreign operations consist of manufacturing facilities located in Belgium, Canada, China, the Dominican Republic, France, Germany, India, Mexico, Morocco, and the United Kingdom, and include sales and service operations located in Brazil, China, and Singapore.&nbsp;&nbsp;For further information regarding foreign operations, see Note&#160;18 to the Consolidated Financial Statements under Item&#160;8 of this report.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">U.S. Government Contracts and Subcontracts</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a contractor and subcontractor to the U.S. government (primarily the DoD), we are subject to various laws and regulations that are more restrictive than those applicable to private sector contractors.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately 3% of our sales was made directly to the U.S. government in fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we estimate that our subcontracting activities to contractors for the U.S. government accounted for approximately 18% of sales during fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;In total, we estimate that approximately 21% of our sales during the fiscal year were subject to U.S. government contracting regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such contracts may be subject to termination, reduction or modification in the event of changes in government requirements, reductions in federal spending, and other factors.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Historically, our U.S. government contracts and subcontracts have been predominately fixed-price contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, fixed-price contracts offer higher margins than cost-plus contracts in return for accepting the risk that increased or unexpected costs may reduce anticipated profits or cause us to sustain losses on the contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;The accuracy and appropriateness of certain costs and expenses used to substantiate our direct and indirect costs for the U.S. government under both cost-plus and fixed-price contracts are subject to extensive regulation and audit by the Defense Contract Audit Agency, an arm of the DoD.&nbsp;&nbsp;The contracts and subcontracts to which we are a party are also subject to profit and cost controls and standard provisions for termination at the convenience of the U.S. government.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon termination, other than for our default, we will normally be entitled to reimbursement for allowable costs and to an allowance for profit.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Trade Compliance Regulations</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are subject to U.S. export laws and regulations, including the ITAR, that generally restrict the export of defense products, technical data, and defense services.&nbsp;&nbsp;On March&#160;5, 2014, the Company entered into a Consent Agreement with the DTCC to resolve alleged ITAR civil violations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Consent Agreement settled the pending ITAR compliance matter with the DTCC previously reported by the Company that resulted from voluntary reports the Company filed with DTCC that disclosed possible technical and administrative violations of the ITAR.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Consent Agreement had a three-year term and provided for:&nbsp;&nbsp;(i)&#160;a payment of $20&#160;million, $10&#160;million of which was suspended and eligible for offset credit based on verified expenditures for past and future remedial compliance measures; (ii)&#160;the appointment of an external Special Compliance Official to oversee compliance with the Consent Agreement and the ITAR; (iii)&#160;two external audits of the Company&#8217;s ITAR compliance program; and (iv)&#160;continued implementation of ongoing compliance measures and additional remedial compliance measures related to automated systems and ITAR compliance policies, procedures, and training.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $10&#160;million portion of the settlement that was not subject to suspension was paid.&nbsp;&nbsp;Compliance expense associated with these measures was $7.1&#160;million in fiscal 2017 and $10.4&#160;million in the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2016, the DTCC approved costs we incurred to implement compliance measures to fully offset the $10&#160;million suspended payment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Consent Agreement was closed in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our trade activities are also subject to customs and border control regulations, anti-bribery and anti-corruption regulations, and regulations that apply to supply chain activities, such as those relating to conflict minerals and the registration, evaluation, authorization and restriction of chemicals, as well as the defense federal acquisition regulations.  Our failure to comply with applicable regulations could result in penalties, loss, or suspension of contracts, breach of contract claims, or other consequences, and the costs to maintain compliance with these regulations may be higher than we anticipate.  Any of these consequences could adversely affect our operations or financial condition.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">7</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU8"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Intellectual Property</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Although we hold a number of patents and licenses, we do not believe that our operations are dependent on our patents and licenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have trademark registrations on our important business names and/or product names filed in key jurisdictions where our businesses operate and sell products.&nbsp;&nbsp;In general, we rely on technical superiority, continual product improvement, exclusive product features, lean manufacturing and operational excellence, including superior lead-time, on-time delivery performance and quality, and customer relationships to maintain competitive advantage.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Seasonality</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The timing of our revenues is impacted by the purchasing patterns of our customers, and as a result we do not generate revenues evenly throughout the year.&nbsp;&nbsp;Moreover, our first fiscal quarter, October through December, includes significant holiday vacation periods in both Europe and North America.&nbsp;&nbsp;This leads to decreased order and shipment activity; consequently, first quarter results are typically weaker than other quarters and not necessarily indicative of our performance in subsequent quarters.&nbsp;&nbsp;Beginning in fiscal 2016, we changed our fiscal year to the twelve months ended the last Friday in September to better align with the aerospace industry&#8217;s business cycle.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sources and Availability of Raw Materials and Components</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The sources and availability of certain raw materials and components are not as critical as they would be for manufacturers of a single product line, due to our vertical integration and diversification.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, certain components, supplies and raw materials for our operations are purchased from single sources.&nbsp;&nbsp;In such instances, we strive to develop alternative sources and design modifications to minimize the effect of business interruptions.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Environmental Matters</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are subject to federal, state, local and foreign laws, regulations and ordinances that (i)&#160;govern activities or operations that may have adverse environmental effects, such as discharges to air and water, as well as handling and disposal practices for solid and hazardous waste, and (ii)&#160;impose liability for the costs of cleaning up, and certain damages resulting from, sites or past spills, disposals or other releases of hazardous substances.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At various times we have been identified as a potentially responsible party pursuant to the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (CERCLA), and analogous state environmental laws, for the cleanup of contamination resulting from past disposals of hazardous wastes at certain sites to which we, among others, sent wastes in the past.&nbsp;&nbsp;CERCLA requires potentially responsible persons to pay for cleanup of sites from which there has been a release or threatened release of hazardous substances.&nbsp;&nbsp;Courts have interpreted CERCLA to impose strict, joint and several liability on all persons liable for cleanup costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a practical matter, however, at sites where there are multiple potentially responsible persons, the costs of cleanup typically are allocated among the parties according to a volumetric or other standard.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have accrued liabilities for environmental remediation costs expected to be incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;Environmental exposures are provided for at the time they are known to exist or are considered probable and estimable.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employees</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We had 13,255 employees at September&#160;29, 2017, of which 4,825 were based in the United States, 4,360 in Europe, 1,498 in Mexico, 981 in Canada, 791 in the Middle East and Asia, 635 in Morocco, and 165 in the Dominican Republic.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately 12% of the U.S.-based employees were represented by labor unions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our non-U.S. operations are subject to union and national trade union agreements and to local regulations governing employment.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financial Information About Foreign and Domestic Operations and Export Sales</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See risk factor below entitled &#8220;Political and economic changes in foreign countries and markets, including foreign currency fluctuations, may have a material effect on our operating results&#8221; under Item&#160;1A of this report and Note&#160;18 to the Consolidated Financial Statements under Item&#160;8 of this report.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Available Information About the Registrant</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU9"></a>You can access financial and other information on our website, <font style="text-decoration:underline;">www.esterline.com</font>.&nbsp;&nbsp;We make available through our website, free of charge, copies of our annual report on Form&#160;10-K, quarterly reports on Form&#160;10-Q, current reports on Form&#160;8-K and amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section&#160;13(a) or Section&#160;15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;), as soon as reasonably practicable after filing such material electronically or otherwise furnishing it to the Securities&#160;and Exchange Commission (SEC).&nbsp;&nbsp;The SEC also maintains a website at <font style="text-decoration:underline;">www.sec.gov</font>, which </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">8</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mr.&#160;Reusser has been Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer since March 2014, and served as President and Chief Executive Officer from October 2013 to March 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Previously, he was President, Aircraft Systems of UTC Aerospace Systems for United Technologies Corporation, a provider of a broad range of high-technology products and services to the global aerospace and building systems industries, from July 2012 to October 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr.&#160;Reusser has a B.S. degree in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering from the University of Washington and a Certificate in Business Management from the University of San Diego.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mr.&#160;George has been Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Development since June 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;From October&#160;2012 to June 2016, he was Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Development.&nbsp;&nbsp;From July&#160;2011 to October&#160;2012, he was Vice President, Chief Financial Officer, Corporate Development and Secretary.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr.&#160;George has an M.B.A. from the Fuqua School of Business at Duke University and a B.A. degree in Economics from Drew University.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mr.&#160;Benson has been Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer since June 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;From April 2015 to June 2016, he was Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to that time, he was Vice President, Human Resources from December 2014 to March 2015 and Senior Director, Human Resources from November 2014 to December 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to that time, he was Senior Human Resources Director at Hewlett Packard Company, a technology products and services company, from 2006 to November 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr.&#160;Benson has an M.B.A. from Arizona State University and a B.A. degree in Business from St. Martin&#8217;s College.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Ms.&#160;Mason has been Executive Vice President and General Counsel since June 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;From September 2013 to June 2016, she was Vice President and General Counsel.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to that time she was General Counsel and Vice President, Administration from August 2012 to September 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Ms.&#160;Mason has a J.D. degree from Northwestern University School of Law and a B.A. degree in Political Science from Portland State University.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mr.&#160;Ross has been Executive Vice President and President, Sensors &amp; Systems since June 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;From August 2015 to June 2016, he was President, Sensors &amp; Systems Segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to that time, he was Senior Vice President, Actuation &amp; Propeller Systems, at UTC Aerospace Systems for United Technologies Corporation, a provider of a broad range of high-technology products and services to the global aerospace and building systems industries, from January 2014 to July 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;From January 2010 to December 2013, he was Vice President, Aerostructures Aftermarket at UTC Aerospace Systems for United Technologies Corporation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr.&#160;Ross has an M.B.A. from the University of Colorado, and M.S. and B.S. degrees in Mechanical Engineering from Colorado State University. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mr.&#160;Yost has been Executive Vice President and President, Advanced Materials and Avionics &amp; Controls since June 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;From August 2015 to June 2016, he was President, Avionics &amp; Controls and Advanced Materials Segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to that time, he was President, Advanced Materials Segment since March 2015 and President, Advanced Materials and Treasurer from March 2014 to February 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;From July&#160;2011 to February&#160;2014, he was Group Vice President and Treasurer.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr.&#160;Yost has an M.B.A. from Utah State University and a B.A. degree in Economics from Brigham Young University.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Additionally, our actual sales and operating earnings may vary from quarter to quarter due to the timing of revenue recognition, sales mix and changes in manufacturing efficiency.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Given these risks and uncertainties, you should not place undue reliance on such forward-looking statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The forward-looking statements included or incorporated by reference into this report are made only as of the date hereof.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not undertake and specifically decline any obligation to update any such statements or to publicly announce the results of any revisions to any such statements to reflect future events or developments.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Item&#160;1A.&#160;&#160;Risk Factors</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Risks Relating to Our Business and Our Industry</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The loss of a significant customer or defense program could have a material adverse effect on our operating results.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Some of our operations are dependent on a relatively small number of customers and aerospace and defense programs, which change from time to time.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant customers in fiscal 2017 included The Boeing Company, Flame, General Electric, Hawker Beechcraft, Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Rolls-Royce, the DoD, and UTC Aerospace Systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurance that our current significant customers will continue to buy our products at current levels.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loss of a significant customer or the cancellation of orders related to a sole-source defense program could have a material adverse effect on our operating results if we were unable to replace the related sales.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our revenues and operating results are subject to fluctuations that may cause our operating results to decline.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our business is susceptible to seasonality, economic cycles and changes to business conditions, and as a result, our operating results have fluctuated widely in the past and are likely to continue to do so.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our revenue tends to fluctuate based on a number of market factors, including domestic and foreign economic conditions and developments affecting the specific industries and customers we serve.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, it is possible that a global recession could occur and result in a more severe downturn in commercial aviation and defense.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, our operating and financial results are impacted by acquisitions, divestitures or adverse business developments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our ability to effectively manage our portfolio of businesses and our business operations as well as respond to business changes will have an impact on our financial and operating results. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">It is also possible that in the future our operating results in a particular quarter or quarters will not meet the expectations of securities analysts or investors, causing the market price of our common stock or senior notes to decline.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that quarter-to-quarter comparisons of our operating results are not a good indication of our future performance and should not be relied upon to predict our future performance.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU11"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We may be unable to realize expected benefits from our business integration efforts and our profitability may be hurt or our business otherwise might be adversely affected.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2014 we began to consolidate certain facilities to create greater cost efficiencies through shared services in sales, general administration and support functions across our segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017 we focused on achieving direct and indirect overhead reductions and improving our operational efficiencies at recently consolidated facilities and creating shared services.&nbsp;&nbsp;These integration activities are intended to generate operating expense savings through direct and indirect overhead expense reductions as well as other savings and realizing these savings may be difficult.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we do not successfully manage our continuing integration activities, or any other similar activities that we may undertake in the future, expected efficiencies and benefits might be delayed or not realized, and our operations and business could be disrupted.&nbsp;&nbsp;Risks associated with these actions include inability to complete or delay in the planned transfer of business activities to other locations due to dependency on third-party agreements or certification of projects affected by the transfer, unanticipated costs in implementing the initiatives, delays in implementation of anticipated workforce reductions, adverse effects on employee morale, creation of customer or supplier uncertainty that may impact our business, and the failure to meet operational targets due to the loss of employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;If any of these risks are realized, our ability to achieve anticipated cost reductions may be impaired or our business may otherwise be harmed, which could have a material adverse effect on our competitive position, results of operations, cash flows or financial condition.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are subject to numerous regulatory requirements for the export and sale of our products and services worldwide that could adversely affect our business.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are also subject to a variety of U.S. and international export control laws and regulations such as the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and ITAR, which generally restrict the export of defense products, technology, technical data and defense services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our trade activities are also subject to international sanctions that significantly restrict or prohibit the sale of certain goods and services in specified countries, including Russia, in which our customers operate or support programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our failure to comply with any of these regulations could result in penalties, loss, or suspension of contracts or other consequences.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we may need to hold shipments or expend significant resources to re-work, re-design or re-certify our products, to achieve compliance with applicable export control regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we are required to take any of these measures, we may lose revenue opportunities, expend significant resources and/or be exposed to late-delivery penalties or other claims from our customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any of these could adversely affect our operations and financial condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;As further described in this report under &#8220;Item 1,&#8221; in September 2017 the Consent Agreement with the DTCC arising from our earlier handling of ITAR-controlled transactions, including the substance of prior voluntary disclosures and other aspects of ITAR compliance errors was closed.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are subject to the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, or FCPA, the U.K. Bribery Act and other anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws that generally prohibit companies and their intermediaries from bribing foreign officials and non-governmental commercial parties for the purpose of obtaining or keeping business or otherwise obtaining favorable treatment.&nbsp;&nbsp;In particular, we may be held liable for actions taken by our strategic or local partners even though our partners are not subject to these laws.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any determination that we have violated the FCPA, the U.K. Bribery Act or similar laws could result in sanctions that could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operation.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our financial performance may be adversely affected by information system business disruptions or failures.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our business may be impacted by information technology attacks or system failures.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cybersecurity attacks, in particular, are evolving and include, but are not limited to, malicious software, attempts to gain unauthorized access to data, and other electronic security breaches that could lead to disruptions in systems, unauthorized release of confidential or otherwise protected information and corruption of data.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have experienced cybersecurity attacks in the past and may experience them in the future, potentially with more frequency.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we have numerous, unique communications, data management and operations support systems across our enterprise that require expertise and significant resources to maintain and upgrade. We have taken measures to mitigate potential risks to our technology information and systems and are implementing plans to modernize and upgrade our systems, in part to comply with U.S. government contracting requirements and with the European Union (EU) General Data Protection Regulation that will become effective in May 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, our plans to upgrade our systems will take time to deploy across our enterprise and the timing, nature and scope of system disruptions and failures are unpredictable.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, we may experience production downtimes, operational delays or other detrimental impacts on our operations or ability to provide products and services to our customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our ability to collect and report financial information from our businesses may be impacted.&nbsp;&nbsp;The compromising of confidential or otherwise protected information, destruction or corruption of data, security breaches, or other manipulation or improper use of our systems or networks could occur.&nbsp;&nbsp; We may also experience financial losses from remedial actions, including significant expenditures to restore or replace systems, loss of business or potential liability under contracts or pursuant to regulations that require us to maintain confidential and other data securely, and/or damage to our reputation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any of these consequences could have a material adverse effect on our competitive position, results of operations, cash flows or financial condition.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">11</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">One of our key strategies is to grow our business by selectively pursuing acquisitions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since 1996 we have completed over 30 acquisitions, and we are continuing to actively pursue additional acquisition opportunities, some of which may be material to our business and financial performance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although we have been successful with this strategy in the past, we may not be able to grow our business in the future through acquisitions for a number of reasons, including:</p>
