<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Failure to continue implementing our acquisition strategy, including successfully integrating acquired businesses, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our future financial results could be adversely impacted by asset impairment charges.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are required to test both acquired goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment on an annual basis based upon a fair value approach, rather than amortizing them over time.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have chosen to perform our annual impairment reviews of goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible assets during the fourth quarter of each fiscal year.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also are required to test goodwill for impairment between annual tests if events occur or circumstances change that would more likely than not reduce our enterprise fair value below its book value.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As we have grown through acquisitions, we have accumulated $1.1&#160;billion of goodwill, $41.4&#160;million of indefinite-lived intangible assets, and $317.8&#160;million of definite-lived intangible assets, out of total assets of $3.1&#160;billion at September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the amount of any annual or interim impairment could be significant and could have a material adverse effect on our reported financial results for the period in which the charge is taken.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We performed our annual impairment review for fiscal 2017 as of July&#160;1, 2017, and our review indicated that no impairment of goodwill or other indefinite-lived assets exists at any of our reporting units.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reductions in defense spending could adversely affect our business.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Approximately 30% of our business is dependent upon defense spending.&nbsp;&nbsp;The defense industry is dependent upon the level of equipment expenditures by the armed forces of countries around the world, and especially those of the United States, which represents a significant portion of worldwide defense expenditures.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reductions in defense spending in 2018 and beyond are possible, which could have significant future consequences to our business, including termination or disruption of programs and personnel reductions that could impact our manufacturing operations and engineering capabilities.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We may have exposure to greater than anticipated tax liabilities and a higher effective tax rate.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are subject to income taxes in the United States and foreign jurisdictions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our effective tax rate is influenced by a number of factors, including, but not limited to, the mix of earnings in countries with differing statutory tax rates, modification on tax policy, interpretation of existing tax laws, and our ability to sustain our reporting positions on examination.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any adverse changes in those factors could have a negative effect on our effective tax rate and financial results.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">12</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU13"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition, the U.S. an</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">d foreign governments have introduced proposals for changes in tax legislation, or have adopted tax laws in response to the guidelines provided by the Organization for Economic Co-Operation and Development to address base erosion and profit shifting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Thes</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">e changes will increase tax uncertainty and may adversely impact our effective tax rate. </font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our operations depend on our production facilities throughout the world.&nbsp;&nbsp;These production facilities are subject to physical and other risks that could disrupt production.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our production facilities could be damaged or disrupted by a natural disaster, war, political unrest, terrorist activity or a pandemic.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, our facilities are subject to local labor conditions that may lead to labor strikes, work stoppages or high levels of employee turnover that could also disrupt our business operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Several of our production facilities are located in California, and thus are in areas with above average seismic activity and may also be at risk of damage in wildfires.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although we have obtained property damage and business interruption insurance for our production facilities, a major catastrophe such as an earthquake or other natural disaster at any of our sites, or significant labor strikes, work stoppage, political unrest, war or terrorist activities in any of the areas where we conduct operations, could result in a prolonged interruption of our business.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any disruption resulting from these events could cause significant delays in shipments of products and the loss of sales and customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We cannot assure you that we will have insurance to adequately compensate us for any of these events.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We may not be able to compete effectively.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our products and services are affected by varying degrees of competition.&nbsp;&nbsp;We compete with other companies and divisions and units of larger companies in most markets we serve, many of which have greater sales volumes or financial, technological or marketing resources than we do.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our principal competitors include:&nbsp;&nbsp;Astronautics, BAE, Bose, Eaton, ECE, Elbit, EMS, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, IAI, L-3, Otto Controls, RAFI, Rockwell Collins, SELEX, Telephonics, Thales, Ultra Electronics, and Universal Avionics Systems Corporation in our Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls segment; Ametek, Amphenol, Eaton, ECE, MPC Products, Meggitt, STPI-Deutsch, and TE Connectivity in our Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems segment; and Chemring, Doncasters, Hi-Temp, J&amp;M, JPR Hutchinson, Kmass, Meggitt (including Dunlop Standard Aerospace Group), Rheinmetall, Trelleborg, ULVA, UMPCO, and UTC Aerospace Systems in our Advanced Materials segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The principal competitive factors in the commercial markets in which we participate are product performance, on-time delivery performance, quality, service and price.&nbsp;&nbsp;Maintaining product performance requires expenditures in research and development that lead to product improvement and new product introduction.&nbsp;&nbsp;Companies with more substantial financial resources may have a better ability to make such expenditures.&nbsp;&nbsp;The business model for some of our businesses is based upon access to the aftermarket and its premium pricing over OEM pricing.&nbsp;&nbsp;The strategic goal of our major OEM customers is to increase their access to the aftermarket from their supplier base, which would correspondingly decrease our sales to aftermarket customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We cannot assure that we will be able to continue to successfully compete in our markets, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The amount of debt we have outstanding, as well as any debt we may incur in the future, could have an adverse effect on our operational and financial flexibility.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of September&#160;29, 2017, we had approximately $759.4&#160;million of long-term debt outstanding, including a credit facility and $17.4&#160;million in current maturities of long-term debt.&nbsp;&nbsp;The credit facility is secured by substantially all of the Company&#8217;s assets.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our level of debt could have significant consequences to our business, including the following:</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Political and economic changes in foreign countries and markets, including foreign currency fluctuations, may have a material effect on our operating results.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU14"></a>Foreign sales originating from non-U.S. locations were approximately 49% of our total sales in fiscal 2017, and we have manufacturing facilities in a number of foreign countries.&nbsp;&nbsp;A substantial portion of our Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls operations is based in Belgium, Canada and the U.K., and a substantial portion of our Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems operations is based in France and the U.K.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also have manufacturing operations in China, the Dominican Republic, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, and Morocco.&nbsp;&nbsp;Doing </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">13</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">business in foreign countries is subject to numerous risks, including political and economic instability, restrictive trade policies of foreign governments, changes in the local labor-relations climate, economic co</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">nditions in local markets, health concerns, inconsistent product regulations or unexpected changes in regulatory and other legal requirements by foreign agencies or governments, the imposition of product tariffs and the burdens of complying with a wide var</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">iety of international and U.S. export laws and differing regulatory requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;U.S. international trade policy is uncertain under the new administration, including, for example, the government&#8217;s decision to renegotiate the North American Free Trade Agr</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">eement, which could cause an increase in customs duties that in turn could adversely affect intercompany transactions among Esterline&#8217;s operating subsidiaries in Canada, Mexico and the U.S., and increase transaction costs with third party suppliers and cus</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">tomers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, the U.K. voter approval of an exit from the EU, known as &#8220;Brexit,&#8221; caused and may continue to cause significant volatility in global stock markets and currency exchange rate fluctuations and may create further global economic uncertainty </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">that may adversely impact the economies of the U.K., the EU and other nations in which we conduct business.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that foreign sales are transacted in a foreign currency, we are subject to the risk of losses due to foreign currency fluctuations.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition, we have substantial assets denominated in foreign currencies, primarily the British pound, Canadian dollar and euro, that are not offset by liabilities denominated in those foreign currencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;These net foreign currency investments are subjec</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">t to material changes in the event of fluctuations in foreign currencies against the U.S. dollar.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A global recession may adversely affect our business operations and results, capital, and cost of capital.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the event of a global recession, our customers may choose to delay or postpone purchases from us until the economy and their businesses strengthen.&nbsp;&nbsp;Decisions by current or future customers to forgo or defer purchases and/or our customers&#8217; inability to pay for our products may adversely affect our earnings and cash flow.&nbsp;&nbsp;A recession could also adversely affect our future cost of debt and equity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any inability to obtain adequate financing from debt and equity sources could force us to self-fund strategic initiatives or even forgo some opportunities, potentially harming our financial position, results of operations, and liquidity. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A downturn in the aircraft market could adversely affect our business.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The aerospace industry is cyclical in nature and affected by periodic downturns that are beyond our control.&nbsp;&nbsp;The principal customers for manufacturers of commercial aircraft are the commercial and regional airlines, which can be adversely affected by a number of factors, including a recession, increasing fuel and labor costs, intense price competition, outbreak of infectious disease and terrorist attacks, as well as economic cycles, all of which can be unpredictable and are outside our control.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any decrease in demand resulting from a downturn in the market could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our backlog is subject to modification or termination, which may reduce our sales in future periods.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We currently have a backlog of orders based on our contracts with customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under many of our contracts, our customers may unilaterally modify or terminate their orders at any time.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the maximum contract value specified under a government contract awarded to us is not necessarily indicative of the sales that we will realize under that contract.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, we are a sole-source prime contractor for many different military programs with the U.S. DoD.&nbsp;&nbsp;We depend heavily on the government contracts underlying these programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Over its lifetime, a program may be implemented by the award of many different individual contracts and subcontracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;The funding of government programs is subject to congressional appropriation.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Changes in defense procurement models may make it more difficult for us to successfully bid on projects as a prime contractor and limit sole-source opportunities available to us.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In recent years the trend in combat system design and development appears to be evolving toward the technological integration of various battlefield components, including combat vehicles, command and control network communications, advanced technology artillery systems and robotics.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the U.S. military procurement approach continues to require this kind of overall battlefield combat system integration, we expect to be subject to increased competition from aerospace and defense companies which have significantly greater resources than we do.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We may lose money or generate less than expected profits on our contracts, including our fixed-price contracts.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU15"></a>Our customers set demanding specifications for product performance, reliability and cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of our government contracts and subcontracts provide for a predetermined, fixed price for the products we make regardless of the costs we incur.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, we must absorb cost overruns, notwithstanding the difficulty of estimating all of the costs we will incur in performing these contracts and in projecting the ultimate level of sales that we may achieve.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our failure to accurately scope the statement of work, anticipate technical problems, estimate costs accurately, integrate technical processes effectively, reduce dependency on sole-source or poor-performing suppliers, control costs or otherwise meet contractual obligations such as timely delivery and meeting quality specifications during performance of a contract may reduce the profitability or cause a loss on the contract.&nbsp;&nbsp;While we believe that we have recorded adequate provisions in our financial statements for losses on our fixed-price and other contracts as required </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">14</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">under GAAP, we cannot assure that our contract loss provisions w</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ill be adequate to cover all actual future losses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, we may incur losses on contracts that we had expected to be profitable, or such contracts may be less profitable than expected.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our business is subject to government contracting regulations, and our failure to comply with such laws and regulations could harm our operating results and prospects.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We estimate that approximately 21% of our sales in fiscal 2017 were attributable to contracts in which we were either the prime contractor to, or a subcontractor to a prime contractor to, the U.S. government.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a contractor and subcontractor to the U.S. government, we must comply with laws and regulations relating to the formation, security, administration and performance of federal government contracts that affect how we do business with our customers and may impose added costs to our business.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, these regulations and laws include provisions that contracts we have been awarded are subject to:</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The accuracy and appropriateness of certain costs and expenses used to substantiate our direct and indirect costs for the U.S. government under both cost-plus and fixed-price contracts are subject to extensive regulation and audit by the Defense Contract Audit Agency, an arm of the U.S. DoD.&nbsp;&nbsp;Responding to governmental audits, inquiries or investigations may involve significant expense and divert management attention.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our failure to comply with these or other government procurement laws and regulations could result in contract termination, suspension or debarment from contracting with the federal government, loss of opportunities to participate in future government programs, civil fines and damages, and criminal prosecution and penalties, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our operating results. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A significant portion of our business depends on U.S. government contracts, which are often subject to competitive bidding, and a failure to compete effectively or accurately anticipate the success of future projects could adversely affect our business.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We obtain many of our U.S. government contracts through a competitive bidding process that subjects us to risks associated with:</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">The design complexity and rapid rate of technological advancement of defense-related products.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition, in order to win the award of developmental programs, we must be able to align our research and development and product offerings with the government&#8217;s changing concepts of national defense and defense systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;The government&#8217;s termination of, or failure to fully fund, one or more of the contracts for our programs would have a negative impact on our operating results and financial condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, we serve as a subcontractor on several military programs that, in large part, involve the same risks as prime contracts.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Overall, we rely on key contracts with U.S. government entities for a significant portion of our sales and business.&nbsp;&nbsp;A substantial reduction in these contracts would materially adversely affect our operating results and financial position.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The market for our products may be affected by our ability to adapt to technological change.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The rapid change of technology is a key feature of all of the markets in which our businesses operate.&nbsp;&nbsp;To succeed in the future, we will need to design, develop, manufacture, assemble, test, market, and support new products and enhancements to our existing products in a timely and cost-effective manner.&nbsp;&nbsp;Historically, our technology has been developed through internal research and development expenditures, as well as customer-sponsored research and development programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is no guarantee that we will continue to maintain, or benefit from, comparable levels of research and development in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, our competitors may develop technologies and products that are more effective than those we develop or that render our technology and products obsolete or noncompetitive.&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, our products could become unmarketable if new industry standards emerge.&nbsp;&nbsp;We cannot assure that our existing products will not require significant modifications in the future to remain competitive or that new products we introduce will be accepted by our customers, nor can we assure that we will successfully identify new opportunities, continue to have the needed financial resources to develop new products in a timely or cost-effective manner or execute on a research and development program effectively to yield expected or any return on investment.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">15</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU16"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The airline industry is heavily regulated and if we fail to comply with applicable requirements, our results of operations could suffer.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Governmental agencies throughout the world, including the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), prescribe standards and qualification requirements for aircraft components, including virtually all commercial airline and general aviation products, as well as regulations regarding the repair and overhaul of aircraft engines.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specific regulations vary from country to country, although compliance with FAA requirements generally satisfies regulatory requirements in other countries.&nbsp;&nbsp;We include, with the replacement parts that we sell to our customers, documentation certifying that each part complies with applicable regulatory requirements and meets applicable standards of airworthiness established by the FAA or the equivalent regulatory agencies in other countries.&nbsp;&nbsp;In order to sell our products, we and the products we manufacture, must also be certified by our individual OEM customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;If any of the material authorizations or approvals qualifying us to supply our products is revoked or suspended, then the sale of the subject product would be prohibited by law, which would have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">From time to time, the FAA or equivalent regulatory agencies in other countries propose new regulations or changes to existing regulations, which are usually more stringent than existing regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;If these proposed regulations are adopted and enacted, we may incur significant additional costs to achieve compliance, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We depend on the continued contributions of our executive officers and other key management, each of whom would be difficult to replace.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our future success depends to a significant degree upon the continued contributions of our senior management and our ability to attract and retain other highly qualified management personnel.&nbsp;&nbsp;We face competition for management from other companies and organizations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, we may not be able to retain our existing management personnel or fill new management positions or vacancies created by expansion or turnover at our existing compensation levels.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although we have entered into change of control agreements with members of senior management, we do not have employment contracts with our key executives, nor have we purchased &#8220;key-person&#8221; insurance on the lives of any of our key officers or management personnel to reduce the impact to our company that the loss of any of them would cause.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specifically, the loss of any of our executive officers would disrupt our operations and divert the time and attention of our remaining officers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, failure to attract and retain highly qualified management personnel would damage our business prospects.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">If we are unable to protect our intellectual property rights adequately, the value of our products could be diminished.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our success is dependent in part on obtaining, maintaining and enforcing our proprietary rights and our ability to avoid infringing on the proprietary rights of others.&nbsp;&nbsp;While we take precautionary steps to protect our technological advantages and intellectual property and rely in part on patent, trademark, trade secret and copyright laws, we cannot assure that the precautionary steps we have taken will completely protect our intellectual property rights.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because patent applications in the United States are maintained in secrecy until either the patent application is published or a patent is issued, we may not be aware of third-party patents, patent applications and other intellectual property relevant to our products that may block our use of our intellectual property or may be used in third-party products that compete with our products and processes.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the event a competitor successfully challenges our products, processes, patents or licenses or claims that we have infringed upon their intellectual property, we could incur substantial litigation costs defending against such claims, be required to pay royalties, license fees or other damages or be barred from using the intellectual property at issue, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, operating results, and financial condition.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition to our patent rights, we also rely on unpatented technology, trade secrets and confidential information.&nbsp;&nbsp;Others may independently develop substantially equivalent information and techniques or otherwise gain access to or disclose our technology.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may not be able to protect our rights in unpatented technology, trade secrets and confidential information effectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;We require each of our employees and consultants to execute a confidentiality agreement at the commencement of an employment or consulting relationship with us.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, these agreements may not provide effective protection of our information or, in the event of unauthorized use or disclosure, they may not provide adequate remedies.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Future asbestos claims could harm our business.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are subject to potential liabilities relating to certain products we manufactured containing asbestos.&#160; We had insurance coverage for asbestos exposures in products prior to November&#160;1, 2003.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since November&#160;1, 2003, insurance coverage for asbestos claims has been unavailable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our policy coverage for exposures prior to November&#160;1, 2003, declines ratably, by formula, as the number of years increases since coverage expired.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, we continue to have partial insurance coverage for exposure to asbestos contained in our products prior to November&#160;1, 2003.&nbsp;&nbsp;To date, asbestos claims have not been material to our consolidated results of operations or financial position.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">16</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU17"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a result of the termination of the NASA Space Shuttle program, manufacturing of rocket engine insulation material containing asbestos ceased in July 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;In December 2011, we dismantled our facility used to manufacture the asbestos-b</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ased insulation for the Space Shuttle program.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have an agreement for indemnification for certain losses we may incur as a result of asbestos claims relating to a product we previously manufactured, but we cannot assure that this indemnification agreeme</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">nt will fully protect us from losses arising from asbestos claims.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">To the extent we are not insured or indemnified for losses from asbestos claims relating to our products, asbestos claims could adversely affect our operating results and our financial condition.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Environmental laws and regulations may subject us to significant liability.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our business and our facilities are subject to a number of federal, state, local and foreign laws, regulations and ordinances governing, among other things, the use, manufacture, storage, handling and disposal of hazardous materials and certain waste products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among these environmental laws are rules by which a current or previous owner or operator of land may be liable for the costs of investigation, removal or remediation of hazardous materials at such property.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, these laws typically impose liability regardless of whether the owner or operator knew of, or was responsible for, the presence of any hazardous materials.&nbsp;&nbsp;Persons who arrange for the disposal or treatment of hazardous materials may be liable for the costs of investigation, removal or remediation of such substances at the disposal or treatment site, regardless of whether the affected site is owned or operated by them.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Because we own and operate, and previously owned and operated, a number of facilities that use, manufacture, store, handle or arrange for the disposal of various hazardous materials, we may incur costs for investigation, removal and remediation, as well as capital costs, associated with compliance with environmental laws.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the time of our asset acquisition of the Electronic Warfare Passive Expendables Division of BAE Systems North America (BAE), certain environmental remedial activities were required under a Part&#160;B Permit issued to the infrared decoy flare facility by the Arkansas Department of Environmental Quality under the Federal Resource Conservation and Recovery Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Part&#160;B Permit was transferred to our subsidiary, Armtec, along with the remedial obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the terms of the asset purchase agreement, BAE agreed to perform and pay for these remedial obligations at the infrared decoy flare facility up to a maximum amount of $25.0&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;BAE is currently conducting monitoring activities as required under the asset purchase agreement.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At the end of fiscal 2017, we had a $2.0&#160;million liability in current liabilities of businesses held for sale related to the removal of hazardous material at our Wallop countermeasure flare facility.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Although environmental costs have not been material in the past, we cannot assure that these matters, or any similar liabilities that arise in the future, will not exceed our resources, nor can we completely eliminate the risk of accidental contamination or injury from these materials.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">An accident at our combustible ordnance or flare countermeasure operations could harm our business.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are subject to potential liabilities in the event of an accident at our combustible ordnance and flare countermeasure operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our products are highly flammable during certain phases of the manufacturing process.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, our facilities are designed to isolate these operations from direct contact with employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our overall safety infrastructure is compliant with regulatory guidelines.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we utilize hazard detection and intervention systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our employees receive safety training and participate in internal safety demonstrations.&nbsp;&nbsp;We continuously track safety effectiveness in relation to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, OSHA, and the HSE in the U.K. to help ensure performance is within industry standards.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we perform on-going process safety hazard analyses, which are conducted by trained safety teams to identify risk areas that arise.&nbsp;&nbsp;We monitor progress through review of safety action reports that are produced as part of our operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although we believe our safety programs are robust and our compliance with our programs is high, it is possible for an accident to occur.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have had incidents in the past, including accidents at our Arkansas plant in 2014 and 2016 and an accident at our Wallop plant in 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The accidents in 2016 resulted in three serious injuries and the closure of our Arkansas plant for approximately 4 months.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are insured in excess of our deductible on losses from property, loss of business, and for personal liability claims from an accident; however, we may not be able to maintain insurance coverage in the future at an acceptable cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant losses not covered by insurance could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We may be required to defend lawsuits or pay damages in connection with the alleged or actual harm caused by our products.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU18"></a>We face an inherent business risk of exposure to product liability claims in the event that the use of our products is alleged to have resulted in harm to others or to property.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, our operations expose us to potential liabilities for personal injury or death as a result of the failure of an aircraft component that has been designed, manufactured or serviced by us.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may incur significant liability if product liability lawsuits against us are successful.&nbsp;&nbsp;While we believe our current general liability and </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">17</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">product liability insurance is adequat</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">e to protect us from future product liability claims, we cannot assure that coverage will be adequate to cover all claims that may arise.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, we may not be able to maintain insurance coverage in the future at an acceptable cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant los</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ses not covered by insurance or for which third-party indemnification is not available could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:9.31%;text-indent:-9.31%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Item&#160;2.&#160;&#160;Properties </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Principal Market &#8211; New York Stock Exchange</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At the end of fiscal 2017, there were approximately 219 holders of record of the Company&#8217;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;On November&#160;16, 2017, there were 217 holders of record of our common stock.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On June&#160;19,&#160;2014, our Board of Directors approved a $200&#160;million share repurchase program.&nbsp;&nbsp;On March&#160;11, 2015, our Board of Directors approved an additional $200 million for the share repurchase program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the program, we are authorized to repurchase up to $400&#160;million of outstanding shares of common stock from time to time, depending on market conditions, share price and other factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;We made no repurchases of common stock during fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to September 29, 2017, we repurchased 37,500 shares of common stock for approximately $2.6&#160;million through November 16, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is $88.9&#160;million available for purchase under our share repurchase program after these recent purchases.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">No cash dividends were paid during fiscal 2017 and 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our current secured credit facility restricts the amount of dividends we can pay.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not anticipate paying any dividends in the foreseeable future.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">EBITDA from continuing operations is a measurement not calculated in accordance with GAAP.&nbsp;&nbsp;We define EBITDA from continuing operations as operating earnings from continuing operations plus depreciation and amortization (excluding amortization of debt issuance costs).&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not intend EBITDA from continuing operations to represent cash flows from continuing operations or any other items calculated in accordance with GAAP, or as an indicator of Esterline&#8217;s operating performance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our definition of EBITDA from continuing operations may not be comparable with EBITDA from continuing operations as defined by other companies.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe EBITDA is commonly used by financial analysts and others in the aerospace and defense industries and thus provides useful information to investors.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our management and certain financial creditors use EBITDA as one measure of our leverage capacity and debt servicing ability, and is shown here with respect to Esterline for comparative purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;EBITDA is not necessarily indicative of amounts that may be available for discretionary uses by us.&nbsp;&nbsp;EBITDA includes goodwill impairment charges of $3,454 in fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The following table reconciles operating earnings from continuing operations to EBITDA from continuing operations:</p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">OVERVIEW</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We operate our businesses in three segments:&nbsp;&nbsp;Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls, Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems and Advanced Materials.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our segments are structured around our technical capabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;All segments include sales to domestic, international, defense and commercial customers.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls segment includes avionics systems, control and communication systems, and interface technologies capabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Avionics systems designs and develops cockpit systems integration and avionics solutions for commercial and military applications and visualization solutions for a variety of demanding defense and commercial aerospace applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;Control and communication systems designs and manufactures technology interface systems for military and commercial aircraft and land- and sea-based military vehicles.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, control and communication systems designs and manufactures military audio and data products for severe battlefield environments and communication control systems to enhance security and aural clarity in military applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interface technologies manufactures and develops custom control panels and input systems for medical, industrial, military and gaming industries.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems segment includes power systems, connection technologies and advanced sensors capabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Power systems develops and manufactures electrical power switching and other related systems, principally for aerospace and defense customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Connection technologies develops and manufactures highly engineered connectors for harsh environments and serves the aerospace, defense&#160;&amp; space, power generation, rail and industrial equipment markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Advanced sensors develops and manufactures high-precision temperature and pressure sensors for aerospace and defense customers.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Advanced Materials segment includes engineered materials and defense technologies capabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Engineered materials develops and manufactures thermally engineered components and high-performance elastomer products used in a wide range of commercial aerospace and military applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;Defense technologies develops and manufactures combustible ordnance components and warfare countermeasure devices for military customers.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our current business and strategic plan focuses on the continued development of products and solutions principally for aerospace and defense markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are concentrating our efforts to expand our capabilities in these markets, anticipate the global needs of our customers and respond to such needs with comprehensive solutions.&nbsp;&nbsp;These efforts focus on continuous research and new product development, acquisitions and strategic realignments of operations to expand our capabilities as a more comprehensive supplier to our customers across our entire product offering.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU23"></a>In March 2014 we entered into a Consent Agreement with the DTCC to resolve alleged ITAR civil violations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among other things, the Consent Agreement required us to pay a $20&#160;million penalty, of which $10&#160;million was suspended and eligible for </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">23</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">offset credit.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In fiscal 2016 the DTCC approved costs we incurred</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> to implement compliance measures to fully offset the $10&#160;million suspended payment.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In fiscal 2017 the Consent Agreement was closed.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In fiscal 2014 our Board of Directors approved the plan to sell certain non-core business units including Eclipse Electronic Systems, Inc. (Eclipse), a manufacturer of embedded communication intercept receivers for signal intelligence applications; Wallop Defence Systems, Ltd. (Wallop), a manufacturer of flare countermeasure devices; a small distribution business; Pacific Aerospace and Electronics Inc. (PA&amp;E), a manufacturer of hermetically sealed electrical connectors; and a small manufacturing business.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of September&#160;30, 2017, we have sold these business units, except for the land and building at Eclipse and Wallop, which are currently held for sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;These businesses are reported as discontinued operations.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In fiscal 2017 we evaluated the on-going performance challenges at our Kirkhill elastomer business, resulting in the decision to explore all strategic options associated with the business. &#160;The historic performance volatility of this business was a consideration in this decision.&#160;&#160;In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017, the results of operations of Kirkhill declined by $10&#160;million from the prior-year period, resulting in a loss of $5&#160;million reflecting lower sales volumes of certain defense products under a new long-term contract which replaced a higher priced product.&#160; For fiscal 2017 the decline was $16&#160;million, resulting in a fiscal year loss of $10&#160;million. The lower priced product is expected to reduce sales by $10&#160;million in fiscal 2018 compared with fiscal 2017.&#160; We are working to offset this impact by decreasing manufacturing expenses through improved efficiency and higher prices on certain commercial contracts.&#160; Kirkhill is included in our Advanced Materials segment.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On June&#160;19, 2014, our Board of Directors approved a share repurchase program and authorized the repurchase of up to $200&#160;million of outstanding shares of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;In March 2015 our Board of Directors authorized an additional $200&#160;million for the repurchase of outstanding shares of common stock under the program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the program, the Company is authorized to repurchase up to $400&#160;million of the outstanding shares of common stock from time to time, depending on market conditions, share price and other factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;There were no shares repurchased during fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2016 we repurchased 304,577 shares under this program at an average price paid per share of $61.51, for an aggregate purchase price of $18.7&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to September 29, 2017, we repurchased 37,500 shares of common stock for approximately $2.6&#160;million through November 16, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is $88.9&#160;million available for purchase under our share repurchase program after these recent purchases.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Consolidated sales for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017 were $531.5&#160;million compared with $543.8&#160;million in the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $12.3&#160;million decrease was mainly due to lower sales for Avionics &amp; Controls segment products of $27.4&#160;million driven by lower demand for defense products and sales in adjacent markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;This decrease was partially offset by higher sales of Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems and Advanced Materials segment products.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in Sensors &amp; Systems reflected strong demand principally for power systems, and the increase in Advanced Materials was mainly due to a recovery of sales of flare countermeasures from an energetic incident at one of our countermeasure operations in the third quarter of fiscal 2016.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Gross margin was 32.9% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017 compared with 35.6% in the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gross margin in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017 was impacted mainly by higher manufacturing costs at Sensors &amp; Systems and lower sales/mix and higher manufacturing costs at Advanced Materials.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For further explanation regarding changes in sales and gross profit in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017 over the prior-year period, please see the table at the end of the Overview section for a roll forward presentation of sales and gross profit.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased by $12.9&#160;million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017 over the prior-year period mainly due to bad debt expense of $9&#160;million in the prior-year for Avionics &amp; Controls segment customers. </p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In fiscal 2017 we received a $7.8&#160;million insurance recovery resulting from an energetic incident at one of our countermeasure operations, which occurred in the third quarter of fiscal 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The incident resulted in injury to two employees, some damage to the building, the destruction of inventory and certain equipment, and the facility was shut down for approximately four months.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also received a $5.0&#160;million insurance recovery in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The insurance recovery is reported as a separate line item on the Consolidated Statement of Operations and Comprehensive Income (Loss) and is included in Advanced Materials segment earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sales and gross margin of our countermeasure operations business continued to be impacted by the controlled restart of operations following the incident through the first half of fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The factory achieved planned production levels in the third quarter of fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not anticipate additional insurance recoveries arising from this matter.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The income tax rate was 27.2% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017 compared with 17.6% in the prior-year period, reflecting U.K. limitations on interest expense deductions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU24"></a>Earnings from continuing operations in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017 were $36.7&#160;million, or $1.22 per diluted share, compared with $52.0&#160;million, or $1.75 per diluted share, in the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Loss from discontinued operations in the </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">24</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">fourth quarter of fiscal 2017 was $1.1&#160;million, or $0.04 per d</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">iluted share, compared with income of $0.2&#160;million, or $0.01 per diluted share, in the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net income in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017 was $35.6&#160;million, or $1.18 per diluted share, compared with $52.3&#160;million, or $1.76 per diluted shar</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">e, in the prior-year period.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sales for fiscal 2017 were $2.002&#160;billion compared to $1.993 billion in the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $9.6&#160;million increase in sales mainly reflected a $30&#160;million increase in Sensors &amp; Systems segment sales, partially offset by a $19&#160;million decrease in Avionics &amp; Controls segment sales.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in Sensors &amp; Systems segment sales was due to higher demand mainly for advanced sensors and power systems products.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in Avionics &amp; Controls segment sales was due to lower demand for defense products and lower sales to adjacent markets.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Consolidated gross margin was 33.2% in both fiscal 2017 and the prior-year period, reflecting strong sales/mix at Sensors &amp; Systems, offset by lower sales/mix and higher manufacturing costs at Advanced Materials mainly from our elastomer business.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Selling, general and administrative expense decreased by $19.9&#160;million to $375.4&#160;million or 18.8% of sales, compared with fiscal 2016, mainly due to decreased bad debt and integration expense of $8&#160;million and $7&#160;million, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Research, development and engineering spending increased by $7.1&#160;million to $103.0&#160;million or 5.1% of sales, compared with fiscal 2016, reflecting higher activity across all segments.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The income tax rate was 23.6% in fiscal 2017 compared with 16.0% in the prior-year period, mainly reflecting U.K. limitations on interest expense deductions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Earnings from continuing operations in fiscal 2017 were $124.7&#160;million, or $4.15 per diluted share, compared with $117.0&#160;million, or $3.93 per diluted share, in the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Loss from discontinued operations in fiscal 2017 was $7.3&#160;million, or $0.24 per diluted share, compared with $15.3&#160;million, or $0.51 per diluted share, in the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net income for fiscal 2017 was $117.4&#160;million, or $3.91 per diluted share, compared with $101.7&#160;million, or $3.42 per diluted share, in the prior-year period.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash flows from operating activities were $193.5&#160;million in fiscal 2017 compared with $167.2&#160;million in the prior-year period, mainly reflecting higher net earnings and cash receipts from the sale of products.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our sales, gross profit and earnings results for the three and twelve month periods ended September&#160;29, 2017, compared with the three and twelve month periods ended September&#160;30, 2016, included a number of significant items which are summarized in the tables below.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest expense was $30.2&#160;million during fiscal 2017, compared with $30.1&#160;million in the prior-year period.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The income tax rates were 23.6% and 16.0% for fiscal 2017 and 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The income tax rate in the current year was higher primarily due to U.K. limitations on interest expense deductions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Both years benefited from various tax credits, certain foreign interest deductions, and lower income tax rates on permanently invested foreign sourced income.&nbsp;&nbsp;The income tax rate in fiscal 2017 and 2016 principally reflected the following discrete income tax items: </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">29</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.52%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.52%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU29"></a><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">During fiscal 2017, we recognized $7.0&#160;mill</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">ion of discrete tax benefits primarily related to a reduction of the income tax rate in France for fiscal year 2020 and beyond and the early adoption of the accounting standard update for employee share-based payment awards</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.52%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">In fiscal 2016, we recognized approximately $3.5 million of discrete tax benefits principally related to the enactment of tax laws reducing the U.K. statutory income tax rate</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We expect the income tax rate to be approximately 27% to 28% in fiscal 2018.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">If enacted, recent proposals to lower the U.S. corporate income tax rate from the current Federal statutory income tax rate of 35% would require us to reduce our net deferred tax assets primarily related to our U.S. post-retirement benefit plan, resulting in a one-time, non-cash increase in income tax expense in the year of enactment.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we would be required to pay one-time cash taxes on the undistributed earnings of our foreign subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;In subsequent years, our income tax expense could be materially reduced.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">It is reasonably possible that within the next twelve months approximately $1.4&#160;million of tax benefits that are currently unrecognized could be recognized as a result of settlement of examinations and/or expiration of a statute of limitations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">New orders for fiscal 2017 were $2.0&#160;billion compared with $2.1&#160;billion for fiscal 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Backlog was $1.3&#160;billion at September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately $440&#160;million is scheduled to be delivered after fiscal 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;Backlog is subject to cancellation until delivery.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fiscal 2016 Compared with Fiscal 2015</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sales for fiscal 2016 decreased by $10.2&#160;million, or 0.5%, from fiscal 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fiscal 2015 benefited from a strong October 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The last Friday in October 2014 was our previous year-end, and in changing our year-end from the last Friday in October to the last Friday in September, October 2014 was included in our recast first fiscal quarter of 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fiscal 2016 consisted of 52 weeks and fiscal 2015 consisted of 53 weeks.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls segment gross margin was 32.8% and 33.8% for fiscal 2016 and 2015, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Segment gross profit was $282.3&#160;million compared with $279.1&#160;million in the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $3&#160;million increase in gross profit mainly reflected the following:</p>
<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">A $2&#160;million write-off of fixed assets due to an avionics systems program realignment in the prior year</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Research, development and engineering spending was $95.9&#160;million, or 4.8% of sales, for fiscal 2016 compared with $100.4&#160;million, or 5.0% of sales, for the prior-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $4.5&#160;million decrease in research, development and engineering principally reflected the following:</p>

<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Total restructuring expenses were $8.7&#160;million, or 0.4% of sales, in fiscal 2016, of which $4.9&#160;million is reported separately as restructuring expenses and $3.8&#160;million is included in cost of goods sold.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total restructuring expenses were $14.6&#160;million, or 0.7% of sales, in fiscal 2015, of which $8.1&#160;million is reported separately as restructuring expenses and $6.5&#160;million is included in cost of goods sold.</p>
