<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Working Capital and Statement of Cash Flows</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash and cash equivalents at the end of fiscal 2017 totaled $307.8&#160;million, an increase of $49.3&#160;million from September&#160;30, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net working capital increased to $887.0&#160;million at the end of fiscal 2016 from $777.3&#160;million at the end of the prior year.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash flows from operating activities were $193.5&#160;million and $167.2&#160;million in fiscal 2017 and 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase principally reflected higher net earnings and cash receipts from the sale of products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sources and uses of cash flows from operating activities principally consisted of cash received from the sale of products and cash payments for material, labor and operating expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU33"></a>Cash flows used by investing activities were $57.4&#160;million and $65.9&#160;million in fiscal 2017 and 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash flows used by investing activities in fiscal 2017 primarily reflected capital expenditures of $58.0&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash flows used by investing activities in fiscal 2016 primarily reflected capital expenditures of $68.5&#160;million, partially offset by proceeds from the </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">33</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">sale of a discontinued operation of $3.7&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Capital expenditures in </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">fiscal 2016 included the purchase of a building for our EAD operation.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash flows used by financing activities were $94.4&#160;million and $29.4&#160;million in fiscal 2017 and 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash flows used by financing activities in fiscal 2017 primarily reflected repayment of long-term debt and credit facilities of $126.4&#160;million, partially offset by $28.1&#160;million from the issuance of common stock under our employee stock plans and $5.0&#160;million in proceeds from our credit facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash flows used by financing activities in fiscal 2016 primarily reflected repayment of long-term debt and credit facilities of $62.4&#160;million, $18.7&#160;million in shares repurchased, partially offset by $6.1&#160;million from the issuance of common stock under our employee stock plans and $45.0&#160;million in proceeds from our credit facilities.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capital Expenditures</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net property, plant and equipment was $348.6&#160;million at September&#160;29, 2017, compared with $338.0&#160;million at September&#160;30, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Capital expenditures for fiscal 2017 and 2016 were $58.0&#160;million and $68.5&#160;million, respectively (excluding acquisitions), and included facilities, machinery, equipment and enhancements to information technology systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;Capital expenditures are anticipated to approximate $82.5&#160;million for fiscal 2018.  The increase in capital expenditures in fiscal 2018 mainly reflects expenditures to support new defense and nuclear programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;We will continue to support expansion through investments in infrastructure including machinery, equipment, and information systems.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Acquisitions</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January&#160;31, 2015, we acquired the defense, aerospace and training display business, or EAD, of Belgium-based Barco N.V. (Barco) for &#8364;150&#160;million, or approximately $171&#160;million, in cash before a working capital adjustment of approximately $15&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The EAD business develops and manufactures visualization solutions for a variety of demanding defense and commercial aerospace applications and is included in our Avionics &amp; Controls segment.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Debt Financing</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">U.S. Credit Facility</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On April&#160;9, 2015, we amended the secured credit facility to extend the expiration to April&#160;9, 2020, increase the revolving credit facility to $500&#160;million, and provide for a delayed-draw term loan facility of $250&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;We recorded $2.3&#160;million in debt issuance costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The credit facility is secured by substantially all the Company&#8217;s assets and interest is based on standard inter-bank offering rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate ranges from LIBOR plus 1.25% to LIBOR plus 2.00%, depending on the leverage ratios at the time the funds are drawn.&nbsp;&nbsp;At September&#160;29, 2017, we had $50.0&#160;million outstanding under the secured credit facility at an interest rate of LIBOR plus 1.50%, which was 2.74%.&nbsp;&nbsp;An additional $27.5&#160;million of unsecured foreign currency credit facilities have been extended by foreign banks for a total of $527.5&#160;million available companywide.&nbsp;&nbsp;Available credit under the above credit facilities was $461.6&#160;million at fiscal 2017 year end, when reduced by outstanding borrowings of $50.0&#160;million and letters of credit of $15.9&#160;million.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">U.S. Term Loan, due April 2020</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On August&#160;3, 2015, we borrowed $250&#160;million under the delayed-draw term loan provided for under the amended credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate on this loan ranges from LIBOR plus 1.25% to LIBOR plus 2.00%, depending on the leverage ratios at the time the funds are drawn.&nbsp;&nbsp;At September&#160;29, 2017, the interest rate was LIBOR plus 1.50%, which equaled 2.74%.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loan amortizes at 1.25% of the original principal balance quarterly through March 2020, with the remaining balance due in April 2020.&nbsp;&nbsp;At September 29, 2017, we had $225.0&#160;million outstanding on the U.S. Term Loan.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3.625% Senior Notes, due April 2023</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In April 2015, we issued &#8364;330.0&#160;million in 3.625% Senior Notes, due April 2023 (2023 Notes) requiring semi-annual interest payments in April and October of each year until maturity.&nbsp;&nbsp;The net proceeds from the sale of the notes, after deducting $5.9&#160;million of debt issuance costs, were $350.8&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2023 Notes are general unsecured senior obligations of the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2023 Notes are unconditionally guaranteed on a senior basis by the Company and certain subsidiaries of the Company that are guarantors under the Company&#8217;s existing secured credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2023 Notes are subject to redemption at the option of the Company at any time prior to April&#160;15, 2018, at a price equal to 100% of the principal amount, plus any accrued interest to the date of redemption and a make-whole provision.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may also redeem up to 35% of the 2023 Notes before April&#160;15, 2018, with the net cash proceeds from equity offerings.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2023 Notes are also subject to redemption at the option of the Company, in whole or in part, on or after April&#160;15, 2018, at redemption prices starting at 102.719% of the principal amount plus accrued interest during the period beginning April&#160;15, 2018, and declining annually to 100% of principal and accrued interest on or after April&#160;15, 2021.&nbsp;&nbsp;At September 29, 2017, we had $389.9 million outstanding on the 2023 Notes.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the redemption of debt in fiscal 2015, we incurred an $8.75&#160;million redemption premium and wrote off $2.7&#160;million in unamortized debt issuance costs as a loss on extinguishment of debt.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">34</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU34"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We believe cash on hand, funds generated from operations and other avai</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">lable debt facilities are sufficient to fund operating cash requirements and capital expenditures through fiscal 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe we will have adequate access to capital markets to fund future acquisitions.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Share Repurchase Program</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On June&#160;19, 2014, our Board of Directors approved a share repurchase program and authorized the repurchase of up to $200&#160;million of outstanding shares of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;In March 2015 our Board of Directors authorized an additional $200&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the program, the Company is authorized to repurchase up to $400&#160;million of the outstanding shares of common stock from time to time, depending on market conditions, share price and other factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2015 we repurchased 2,562,122 shares under this program at an average price paid per share of $101.29, for an aggregate purchase price of $259.5&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2016 we repurchased 304,577 shares under this program at an average price paid per share of $61.51, for an aggregate purchase price of $18.7&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;There were no shares repurchased during fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to September&#160;29, 2017, we repurchased 37,500 shares of common stock for approximately $2.6&#160;million through November 16, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is $88.9&#160;million available for purchase under our share repurchase program after these recent purchases.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Permanent Investment of Undistributed Earnings of Foreign Subsidiaries</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our non-U.S. subsidiaries have $300.4&#160;million in cash and cash equivalents at September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash and cash equivalents at our U.S. parent and subsidiaries aggregated $7.4&#160;million at September&#160;29, 2017, and cash flow from these operations and credit facilities are sufficient to fund working capital, capital expenditures, acquisitions and debt repayments of our domestic operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have available credit to our U.S. parent and subsidiaries of $434.5&#160;million under our U.S. secured credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;The earnings of our non-U.S. subsidiaries are considered to be indefinitely invested, and accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes has been made on accumulated earnings of foreign subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of the unrecognized deferred income tax liability for temporary differences related to investments in foreign subsidiaries is not practical to determine because of the complexities regarding the calculation of unremitted earnings and the potential for tax credits.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Government Refundable Advances</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Government refundable advances consist of payments received from the Canadian government to assist in the research and development related to commercial aviation that is conducted at our Canadian operations, CMC Electronics, Inc. (CMC).&nbsp;&nbsp;These advances totaled $45.5&#160;million and $45.0&#160;million at September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The repayment of the advances is based on year-over-year commercial aviation revenue growth at CMC beginning in 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Imputed interest on the advances was 2.5% at September&#160;29, 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pension and Other Post-Retirement Benefit Obligations</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our pension plans principally include a U.S. pension plan maintained by Esterline, non-U.S. plans maintained by CMC, and other non-U.S. plans.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our principal post-retirement plans include non-U.S. plans maintained by CMC, which are non-contributory health care and life insurance plans.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We account for pension expense using the end of the fiscal year as our measurement date, and we make actuarially computed contributions to our pension plans as necessary to adequately fund benefits.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our funding policy is consistent with the minimum funding requirements of ERISA.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2017 and 2016, operating cash flow included $5.3&#160;million and $10.6&#160;million, respectively, of cash funding to the non-U.S. pension plans maintained primarily by CMC.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is no funding requirement for fiscal 2018 for the U.S. pension plans maintained by Esterline.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect pension funding requirements for the CMC pension plans and other non-U.S. pension plans to be approximately $4.9&#160;million in fiscal 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;The rate of increase in future compensation levels is consistent with our historical experience and salary administration policies.&nbsp;&nbsp;The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets is based on long-term target asset allocations of 70% equity and 30% fixed income.&nbsp;&nbsp;We periodically review allocations of plan assets by investment type and evaluate external sources of information regarding long-term historical returns and expected future returns for each investment type, and accordingly, believe a 3.25% to 8.25% assumed long-term rate of return on plan assets is appropriate for the pension plans.&nbsp;&nbsp;Current allocations are consistent with the long-term targets.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We made the following assumptions with respect to our Esterline pension obligation in fiscal 2017 and 2016:</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We use a discount rate for expected returns that is a spot rate developed from a yield curve established from high-quality corporate bonds and matched to plan-specific projected benefit payments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although future changes to the discount rate are unknown, had the discount rate increased or decreased by 25 basis points in fiscal 2017, pension liabilities in total would have decreased $13.7&#160;million or increased $14.4&#160;million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;If all other assumptions are held constant, the estimated effect on fiscal 2017 pension expense from a hypothetical 25 basis points increase or decrease in both the discount rate and expected long-term rate of return on plan assets would not have a material effect on our pension expense.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The assumed health care trend rate can have a significant impact on our post-retirement benefit obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our health care trend rate was based on the experience of our plan and expectations for the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;A 100 basis points increase in the health care trend rate would increase our post-retirement benefit obligation by $1.4&#160;million at September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;A 100 basis points decrease in the health care trend rate would decrease our post-retirement benefit obligation by $1.2&#160;million at September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Assuming all other assumptions are held constant, the estimated effect on fiscal 2017 post-retirement benefit expense from a hypothetical 100 basis points increase or decrease in the health care trend rate would not have a material effect on our post-retirement benefit expense.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Research and Development Expense</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For the three years ended September&#160;29, 2017, research and development expense averaged 5.0% of sales.&nbsp;&nbsp;We estimate that research and development expense in fiscal 2018 will be approximately 5.0% of sales for the full year.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">36</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Seasonality</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The timing of our revenues is impacted by the purchasing patterns of our customers and, as a result, we do not generate revenues evenly throughout the year.&nbsp;&nbsp;Moreover, our first fiscal quarter, October through December, includes significant holiday vacation periods in both Europe and North America.&nbsp;&nbsp;This leads to decreased order and shipment activity; consequently, first quarter results are typically weaker than other quarters and not necessarily indicative of our performance in subsequent quarters.&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective fiscal 2016, we changed our fiscal year to the twelve months ended the last Friday of September to better align with the aerospace industry&#8217;s business cycle.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Disclosures About Market Risk</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest Rate Risks</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our debt includes fixed rate and variable rate obligations at September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our ratio of fixed and variable rate to total obligations was 59% and 41%, respectively at September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are not subject to interest rate risk on the fixed rate obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are subject to interest rate risk on the U.S. Term Loan and U.S. credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;For long-term debt, the table below presents principal cash flows and the related weighted-average interest rates by contractual maturities.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A hypothetical 10% increase or decrease in average market rates would not have a material effect on our pretax income.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Currency Risks</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU37"></a>We own significant operations in Canada, France and the United Kingdom.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that sales are transacted in a foreign currency, we are subject to foreign currency fluctuation risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, we have assets denominated in foreign currencies that are not offset by liabilities in such foreign currencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;At September&#160;29, 2017, we had the following monetary assets subject to foreign currency fluctuation risk:&nbsp;&nbsp;U.S. dollar-denominated backlog with customers whose functional currency is other than the U.S. dollar; U.S. dollar-denominated accounts receivable and payable; and certain forward contracts, which are </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">37</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">not accounted for as a cash flow hedge.&nbsp;&nbsp;The foreign exchange rate for the dollar relative to the euro decreased to 0.846 at September&#160;29, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, from 0.890 at September&#160;30, 2016; the dollar relative to the British pound decreased to 0.746 from 0.771; and the dollar relative to the Canadian dollar decreased to 1.247 from 1.313.&nbsp;&nbsp;Foreign currency transactions affecting monetary assets, forward cont</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">racts and backlog resulted in an $11.9&#160;million loss in fiscal 2017, a $19.8&#160;million loss in fiscal 2016, and a $1.3&#160;million gain in fiscal 2015.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our policy is to hedge a portion of our forecasted transactions and a portion of our net monetary assets, including the embedded derivatives in our backlog, using forward exchange contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not enter into any forward contracts for trading purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;At September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016, the notional value of foreign currency forward contracts was $411.0&#160;million and $451.3&#160;million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The notional value of our foreign currency forward contracts include $70&#160;million related to the hedge of a portion of our net monetary assets, including the embedded derivatives in our backlog.&nbsp;&nbsp;The net fair value of our open foreign currency forward contracts was an $11.3&#160;million asset and an $11.5&#160;million liability at September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the U.S. dollar increased by a hypothetical 5%, the effect on the fair value of the foreign currency contracts at September&#160;29, 2017, would be a decrease in the net liability of $18.6&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the U.S. dollar decreased by a hypothetical 5%, the effect on the fair value of the foreign currency contracts would be an increase in net liability of $21.6&#160;million.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following tables provide information about our significant derivative financial instruments, including foreign currency forward exchange agreements and certain firmly committed sales transactions denominated in currencies other than the functional currency at September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The information about certain firmly committed sales contracts and derivative financial instruments is in U.S. dollar equivalents.&nbsp;&nbsp;For forward foreign currency exchange agreements, the following tables present the notional amounts at the current exchange rate and weighted-average contractual foreign currency exchange rates by contractual maturity dates.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Critical Accounting Policies</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our financial statements and accompanying notes are prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp;&nbsp;Preparing financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results may differ from estimates under different assumptions or conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;These estimates and assumptions are affected by our application of accounting policies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our critical accounting policies include revenue recognition, accounting for the allowance for doubtful accounts receivable, accounting for inventories, impairment of goodwill and intangible assets, impairment of long-lived assets, accounting for assets held for sale, accounting for legal contingencies, accounting for pension benefits, and accounting for income taxes.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Revenue Recognition</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We recognize revenue when the title and risk of loss have passed to the customer, there is persuasive evidence of an agreement, delivery has occurred or services have been rendered, the price is determinable, and the collectability is reasonably assured.&nbsp;&nbsp;We recognize product revenues at the point of shipment or delivery in accordance with the terms of sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sales are net of returns and allowances.&nbsp;&nbsp;Returns and allowances are not significant because products are manufactured to customer specification and are covered by the terms of the product warranty.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Revenues and profits on fixed-price contracts with significant engineering as well as production requirements are recorded based on the achievement of contractual milestones and the ratio of total actual incurred costs to date to total estimated costs for each contract (cost-to-cost method).&nbsp;&nbsp;We review cost performance and estimates to complete on our ongoing contracts at least quarterly.&nbsp;&nbsp;The impact of revisions of profit estimates are recognized on a cumulative catch-up basis in the period in which the revisions are made.&nbsp;&nbsp;Provisions for anticipated losses on contracts are recorded in the period they become evident.&nbsp;&nbsp;When change orders have been approved by both the Company and the customer for both scope and price and realization is deemed probable, the original contract price is adjusted and revenues are recognized on contract performance (as determined by the achievement of contractual milestones and the cost-to-cost method).&nbsp;&nbsp;For partially approved change orders, costs attributable to unpriced change orders are treated as costs of the contract performance in the period the costs are incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;Claims are also recognized as contract revenue when approved by both the Company and the customer, based on contract performance.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Allowance for Doubtful Accounts</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We establish an allowance for doubtful accounts for losses expected to be incurred on accounts receivable balances.&nbsp;&nbsp;Judgment is required in estimation of the allowance and is based upon specific identification, collection history and creditworthiness of the debtor.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Inventories</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We account for inventories on a first-in, first-out or average cost method of accounting at the lower of its cost or market.&nbsp;&nbsp;The determination of market requires judgment in estimating future demand, selling prices and cost of disposal.&nbsp;&nbsp;Judgment is required when determining inventory cost adjustments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Inventory cost adjustments are recorded when inventory is considered to be excess or obsolete based upon an analysis of actual on-hand quantities on a part-level basis relative to forecasted product demand and historical usage.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Impairment of Goodwill and Intangible Assets</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets are required to be tested for impairment at least annually.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are also required to test goodwill for impairment between annual tests if events occur or circumstances change that would more likely than not reduce our enterprise fair value below its book value.&nbsp;&nbsp;These events or circumstances could include a significant change in the business climate, including a significant sustained decline in an entity&#8217;s market value, legal factors, operating performance indicators, competition, sale or disposition of a significant portion of the business, or other factors.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill is tested for impairment in a two-step process.&nbsp;&nbsp;The first step (Step&#160;One) of the goodwill impairment test involves estimating the fair value of a reporting unit.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value (Fair Value) is defined as &#8220;the amount at which an asset (or liability) could be bought (or incurred) or sold (or settled) in a current transaction between willing parties, that is, other than in a forced liquidation sale.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;A reporting unit is generally defined at the operating segment level or at the component level one level below the operating segment, if said component constitutes a business.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Fair Value of a reporting unit is then compared to its carrying value, which is defined as the book basis of equity plus debt.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the event a reporting unit&#8217;s carrying value exceeds its estimated Fair Value, evidence of potential impairment exists.&nbsp;&nbsp;In such a case, the second step (Step&#160;Two) of the impairment test is required, which involves allocating the Fair Value of the reporting unit to all of the assets and liabilities of that unit, with the excess of Fair Value over allocated net assets representing the Fair Value of goodwill.&nbsp;&nbsp;An impairment loss is measured as the amount by which the carrying value of the reporting unit&#8217;s goodwill exceeds the estimated Fair Value of goodwill.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">41</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU41"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As we have grown through acquisitions, we have accumulated $1.1&#160;billion of goodw</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ill and $41.4&#160;million of indefinite-lived intangible assets out of total assets of $3.1&#160;billion at September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of any annual or interim impairment could be significant and could have a material adverse effect on our reported financial r</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">esults for the period in which the charge is taken.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We performed our annual impairment review for fiscal 2017 as of July&#160;1,&#160;2017, and our Step&#160;One analysis indicates that no impairment of goodwill or other indefinite-lived assets exists at any of our reporting units.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our avionics systems reporting unit&#8217;s margin in passing the Step One analysis was approximately 11%.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is possible, however, that as a result of events or circumstances, we could conclude at a later date that goodwill of $240.2&#160;million at avionics systems may be considered impaired.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also may be required to record an earnings charge or incur unanticipated expenses if, due to a change in strategy or other reasons, we determine the value of other assets has been impaired.&nbsp;&nbsp;These other assets include trade names of $21.3&#160;million and intangible assets of $77.1&#160;million.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The valuation of reporting units requires judgment in estimating future cash flows, discount rates and estimated product life cycles.&nbsp;&nbsp;In making these judgments, we evaluate the financial health of the business, including such factors as industry performance, changes in technology and operating cash flows.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We used available market data and a discounted cash flow analysis in completing our 2017 annual impairment test.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that our cash flow estimates are reasonable based upon the historical cash flows and future operating and strategic plans of our reporting units.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to cash flow estimates, our valuations are sensitive to the rate used to discount cash flows and future growth assumptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of all our other reporting units exceeds its book value by greater than 33%.&nbsp;&nbsp;A 0.5% change in the discount rate used in the cash flow analysis would result in a change in the fair value of our other reporting units of approximately $149.9&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;A 0.5% change in the growth rate assumed in the calculation of the terminal value of cash flows would result in a change in the fair value of our other reporting units by $103.6&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;None of these changes would have resulted in any of our other reporting units being impaired.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Long-lived assets that are to be disposed of are required to be reported at the lower of its carrying amount or fair value less cost to sell.&nbsp;&nbsp;An asset (other than goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets) is considered impaired when estimated future cash flows are less than the carrying amount of the asset.&nbsp;&nbsp;The first step (Step&#160;One) of an impairment test of long-lived assets is to determine the amount of future undiscounted cash flow of the long-lived asset.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the event the undiscounted future cash flow is less than the carrying amount of the long-lived asset, a second step is required (Step&#160;Two), and the long-lived asset is adjusted to its estimated fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value is generally determined based upon estimated discounted future cash flows.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As we have grown through acquisitions, we have accumulated $317.8&#160;million of definite-lived intangible assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of any annual or interim impairment could be significant and could have a material adverse effect on our reported financial results for the period in which the charge is taken.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets Held for Sale </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets held for sale are to be reported at the lower of its carrying amount or fair value less cost to sell.&nbsp;&nbsp;Judgment is required in estimating the sales price of assets held for sale and the time required to sell the assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;These estimates are based upon available market data and operating cash flows of the assets held for sale.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In fiscal 2014, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved a plan to sell certain non-core business units including Wallop Defence Systems, Ltd., a small manufacturing business and a small distribution business.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, we recorded an after-tax loss of $2.9&#160;million, $8.4&#160;million and $31.2&#160;million in fiscal 2017, 2016, and 2015, respectively, on assets held for sale in discontinued operations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Contingencies </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are party to various lawsuits and claims, both as plaintiff and defendant, and have contingent liabilities arising from the conduct of business.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are covered by insurance for general liability, product liability, workers&#8217; compensation and certain environmental exposures, subject to certain deductible limits.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are self-insured for amounts less than our deductible and where no insurance is available.&nbsp;&nbsp;An estimated loss from a contingency should be accrued by a charge to income if it is probable that an asset has been impaired or a liability has been incurred and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Disclosure of a contingency is required if there is at least a reasonable possibility that a loss has been incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;We evaluate, among other factors, the degree of probability of an unfavorable outcome and the ability to make a reasonable estimate of the amount of loss.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pension and Other Post-Retirement Benefits </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU42"></a>We account for pension expense using the end of the fiscal year as our measurement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;We select appropriate assumptions including discount rate, rate of increase in future compensation levels and assumed long-term rate of return on plan assets and </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">42</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">expected annual increases in costs of medical and other health care benefits in regard to our post-retirement benefit obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our assumptions are based upon historical results, the curre</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">nt economic environment and reasonable expectations of future events.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results which vary from our assumptions are accumulated and amortized over future periods, and accordingly, are recognized in expense in these periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant differences b</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">etween our assumptions and actual experience or significant changes in assumptions could impact the pension costs and the pension obligation.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income Taxes </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The objectives of accounting for income taxes are to recognize the amount of taxes payable or refundable for the current year and deferred tax liabilities and assets for the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in our financial statements or tax returns.&nbsp;&nbsp;Judgment is required in assessing the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in our financial statements or tax returns.&nbsp;&nbsp;Variations in the actual outcome of these future tax consequences could materially impact our financial position and results of operations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:9.58%;text-indent:-9.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:9.58%;text-indent:-9.58%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Item&#160;7A.&#160;&#160;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We hereby incorporate by reference the information set forth under the section &#8220;Disclosures About Market Risk&#8221; under Item&#160;7.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:9.58%;text-indent:-9.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">43</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:9.58%;text-indent:-9.58%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU43"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Item&#160;8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Consolidated Statement of Operations</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In Thousands, Except Per Share Amounts</p>
