<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s embedded derivatives are the result of entering into sales or purchase contracts that are denominated in a currency other than the Company&#8217;s functional currency or the supplier&#8217;s or customer&#8217;s functional currency.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value is determined by calculating the difference between quoted exchange rates at the time the contract was entered into and the period-end exchange rate.&nbsp;&nbsp;These contracts are categorized as Level&#160;2 in the fair value hierarchy.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s derivative contracts consist of foreign currency exchange contracts and, from time to time, interest rate swap agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;These derivative contracts are over the counter and their fair value is determined using modeling techniques that include market inputs such as interest rates, yield curves, and currency exchange rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;These contracts are categorized as Level&#160;2 in the fair value hierarchy.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s Board of Directors previously approved a plan to sell certain non-core business units.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon the estimated fair values, the Company adjusted the carrying value of the assets and liabilities of the businesses to fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Principle assumptions used in measuring the estimated value of assets and liabilities held for sale included estimated selling price of the discontinued business, discount rates, industry growth rates, and pricing of comparable transactions in the market.&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;text-transform:uppercase;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-variant: normal;">NOTE&#160;9:&#160;&#160;<font style="font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;">Derivative Financial Instruments</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company may use derivative financial instruments in the form of foreign currency forward exchange contracts and interest rate swap contracts for the purpose of minimizing exposure to changes in foreign currency exchange rates on business transactions and interest rates, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#8217;s policy is to execute such instruments with banks the Company believes to be credit worthy and not to enter into derivative financial instruments for speculative purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;These derivative financial instruments do not subject the Company to undue risk, as gains and losses on these instruments generally offset gains and losses on the underlying assets, liabilities, or anticipated transactions that are being hedged.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All derivative financial instruments are recorded at fair value in the Consolidated Balance Sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;For a derivative that has not been designated as an accounting hedge, the change in the fair value is recognized immediately through earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;For a derivative that has been designated as an accounting hedge of an existing asset or liability (a fair value hedge), the change in the fair value of both the derivative and underlying asset or liability is recognized immediately through earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;For a derivative designated as an accounting hedge of an anticipated transaction (a cash flow hedge), the change in the fair value is recorded on the Consolidated Balance Sheet in Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI) to the extent the derivative is effective in mitigating the exposure related to the anticipated transaction.&nbsp;&nbsp;The change in the fair value related to the ineffective portion of the hedge, if any, is immediately recognized in earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount recorded within AOCI is reclassified into earnings in the same period during which the underlying hedged transaction affects earnings.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair values of derivative instruments are presented on a gross basis, as the Company does not have any derivative contracts which are subject to master netting arrangements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not have any derivative instruments with credit-risk-related contingent features or that required the posting of collateral as of September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cash flows from derivative contracts are recorded in operating activities in the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreign Currency Forward Exchange Contracts</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company transacts business in various foreign currencies which subjects the Company&#8217;s cash flows and earnings to exposure related to changes in foreign currency exchange rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;These exposures arise primarily from purchases or sales of products and services from third parties.&nbsp;&nbsp;Foreign currency forward exchange contracts provide for the purchase or sale of foreign currencies at specified future dates at specified exchange rates, and are used to offset changes in the fair value of certain assets or liabilities or forecasted cash flows resulting from transactions denominated in foreign currencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016, the Company had outstanding foreign currency forward exchange contracts principally to sell U.S. dollars with notional amounts of $406.9&#160;million and $450.9&#160;million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;These notional values consist primarily of contracts for the British pound sterling, Canadian dollar and European euro, and are stated in U.S. dollar equivalents at spot exchange rates at the respective dates.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">64</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU63"></a><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest Rate Swaps</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company manages its exposure to interest rate risk by maintaining an appropriate mix of fixed and variable rate debt, which over time should moderate the costs of debt financing.&nbsp;&nbsp;When considered necessary, the Company may use financial instruments in the form of interest rate swaps to help meet this objective.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Embedded Derivative Instruments</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s embedded derivatives are the result of entering into sales or purchase contracts that are denominated in a currency other than the Company&#8217;s functional currency or the supplier&#8217;s or customer&#8217;s functional currency.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net Investment Hedge</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In April 2015 the Company issued &#8364;330.0&#160;million in 3.625% Senior Notes due April 2023 (2023 Notes) and requiring semi-annual interest payments in April and October each year until maturity.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company designated the 2023 Notes and accrued interest as a hedge of the investment in certain foreign business units.&nbsp;&nbsp;The foreign currency gain or loss that is effective as a hedge is reported as a component of other comprehensive income (loss) in shareholders&#8217; equity.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that this hedge is ineffective, the foreign currency gain or loss is recorded in earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;There was no ineffectiveness since inception of the hedge.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair Value of Derivative Instruments</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU64"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During fiscal 2017 and 2016, the Company recorded a gain of $</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">5.8</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">million and a loss of $6.1&#160;million, respectively, on foreign currency forward exchange contracts that have not been designated as an accounting hedge.&nbsp;&nbsp;These foreign currency exchange gains (losses) are included in selling, general and administrative expen</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">se.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There was no significant impact to the Company&#8217;s earnings related to the ineffective portion of any hedging instruments during fiscal 2017 and 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, there was no significant impact to the Company&#8217;s earnings when a hedged firm commitment no longer qualified as a fair value hedge or when a hedged forecasted transaction no longer qualified as a cash flow hedge during fiscal 2017 and 2016.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Amounts included in AOCI are reclassified into earnings when the hedged transaction settles.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company expects to reclassify approximately $10.9&#160;million of net gain into earnings in fiscal year 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;The maximum duration of a foreign currency cash flow hedge contract at September&#160;29, 2017, is 24 months.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company operates in numerous taxing jurisdictions and is subject to regular examinations by various U.S. federal, state and foreign jurisdictions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the Company assumed tax liabilities and the rights to tax refunds in connection with various acquisitions and divestitures of businesses in prior years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#8217;s income tax positions are based on research and interpretations of income tax laws and rulings in each of the jurisdictions in which the Company does business.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to the subjectivity and complexity of the interpretations of the tax laws and rulings in each jurisdiction, the differences and interplay in the tax laws between those jurisdictions, as well as the inherent uncertainty in estimating the final resolution of complex tax audit matters, the Company&#8217;s estimates of income tax liabilities and assets may differ from actual payments, assessments or refunds.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management believes that it is more likely than not that the Company will realize the benefit of most of its deferred tax assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant factors management considered in determining the probability of the realization of the deferred tax assets include expected future earnings and the reversal of deferred tax liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, no valuation allowance has been recorded on the deferred tax assets other than certain tax credits, capital losses and net operating losses.&nbsp;&nbsp;The U.S. federal capital loss carryforward will begin to expire in fiscal 2020 if not utilized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The foreign net operating loss can be carried forward indefinitely.&nbsp;&nbsp;The majority of the tax credit carryforwards can be carried forward indefinitely.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">U.S. and various state and foreign income tax returns are open to examination, and presently there are foreign and state income tax returns under examination.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such examinations could result in challenges to tax positions taken, and accordingly, the Company may record adjustments to provisions based on the outcomes of such matters.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the Company believes that the resolution of these matters, after considering amounts accrued, will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The incremental tax benefit received by the Company upon exercise of non-qualified employee stock options was $2.1&#160;million, $0.6&#160;million, and $2.0&#160;million in fiscal 2017, 2016, and 2015, respectively.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">67</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The increase in the year-over-year effective tax rate for fiscal 2017 is primarily attributable to the foreign tax law change that limits the interest expense deduction.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase is partially offset by the French tax law change that reduced its corporate income tax rate.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">No provision for federal income taxes has been made on accumulated earnings of foreign subsidiaries, since such earnings are considered indefinitely reinvested.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of undistributed foreign earnings which are considered to be indefinitely reinvested at September&#160;29, 2017, is approximately $669.1&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, the Company determined it was not practical to estimate the deferred taxes on these earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of deferred income taxes is not practical to compute due to the complexity of the Company&#8217;s international holding company structure, layers of regulatory requirements that have to be evaluated to determine the amount of allowable dividends, numerous potential repatriation scenarios that could be created to facilitate the repatriation of earnings to the U.S., and the complexity of computing foreign tax credits.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&nbsp;</p></td>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">U.S. Credit Facility</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On April&#160;9, 2015, the Company amended the secured credit facility to extend the expiration to April&#160;9, 2020, increase the revolving credit facility to $500&#160;million, and provide for a delayed-draw term loan facility of $250&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recorded $2.3&#160;million in debt issuance costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The credit facility is secured by substantially all the Company&#8217;s assets, and interest is based on standard inter-bank offering rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate ranges from LIBOR plus 1.25% to LIBOR plus 2.00%, depending on the leverage ratios at the time the funds are drawn.&nbsp;&nbsp;At September&#160;29, 2017, the Company had $50.0&#160;million outstanding under the secured credit facility at an interest rate of LIBOR plus 1.50%, which was 2.74%.&nbsp;&nbsp;An additional $27.5 million of unsecured foreign currency credit facilities have been extended by foreign banks for a total of $527.5&#160;million available companywide.&nbsp;&nbsp;Available credit under the above credit facilities was $461.6&#160;million at fiscal 2017 year end, when reduced by outstanding borrowings of $50.0&#160;million and letters of credit of $15.9&#160;million.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">U.S. Term Loan, due April 2020</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On August&#160;3, 2015, the Company borrowed $250&#160;million under the delayed-draw term loan provided for under the amended credit facility (U.S. Term Loan, due 2020).&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate on the U.S. Term Loan, due 2020, ranges from LIBOR plus 1.25% to LIBOR plus 2.00%, depending on the leverage ratios at the time the funds are drawn.&nbsp;&nbsp;At September&#160;29, 2017, the interest rate was LIBOR plus 1.50%, which equaled 2.74%.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loan amortizes at 1.25% of the original principal balance quarterly through March 2020, with the remaining balance due in April 2020.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3.625% Senior Notes, due April 2023</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In April 2015 TA Mfg. Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, issued &#8364;330.0&#160;million in 3.625% Senior Notes, due April 2023 (2023 Notes) requiring semi-annual interest payments in April and October of each year until maturity.&nbsp;&nbsp;The net proceeds from the sale of the notes, after deducting $5.9&#160;million of debt issuance costs, were $350.8&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2023 Notes are general unsecured senior obligations of the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2023 Notes are unconditionally guaranteed on a senior basis by the Company and certain subsidiaries of the Company that are guarantors under the Company&#8217;s existing secured credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2023 Notes are subject to redemption at the option of the Company at any time prior to April&#160;15, 2018, at a price equal to 100% of the principal amount, plus any accrued interest to the date of redemption and a make-whole provision.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company may also redeem up to 35% of the 2023 Notes before April&#160;15, 2018, with the net cash proceeds from equity offerings.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2023 Notes are also subject to redemption at the option of the Company, in whole or in part, on or after April&#160;15, 2018, at redemption prices starting at 102.719% of the principal amount plus accrued interest during the period beginning April&#160;15, 2018, and declining annually to 100% of principal and accrued interest on or after April&#160;15, 2021.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU68"></a>Based on quoted market prices, the fair value of the Company&#8217;s 2023 Notes was $403.2&#160;million and $365.3 million as of September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The carrying amounts of the secured credit facility and the U.S. Term </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">69</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loan, due 2020, approximate fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The estimate of fair value for the 2023 Notes was based on Level&#160;2 inputs as defined in the fair value hierarchy.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the redemption of debt in fiscal 2015, the Company incurred an $8.75 million redemption premium and wrote off $2.7 million in unamortized debt issuance costs as a loss on extinguishment of debt.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Government Refundable Advances</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Government refundable advances consist of payments received from the Canadian government to assist in research and development related to commercial aviation based at our Canadian operation, CMC.&nbsp;&nbsp;The repayment of this advance is based on year-over-year commercial aviation revenue growth at CMC beginning in 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Imputed interest on the advance was 2.5% at September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The debt recognized was $45.5&#160;million and $45.0&#160;million as of September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Obligation Under Capital Lease</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company leases building and equipment under capital leases.&nbsp;&nbsp;The present value of the minimum capital lease payments, net of the current portion, totaled $69.0&#160;million as of September&#160;29, 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of September&#160;29, 2017, aggregate annual maturities of long-term debt and future non-cancelable minimum lease payments under capital lease obligations were as follows:</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-right:0.19%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is a party to various lawsuits and claims, both as plaintiff and defendant, and has contingent liabilities arising from the conduct of business, none of which, in the opinion of management, is expected to have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s financial position or results of operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company believes that it has made appropriate and adequate provisions for contingent liabilities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.19%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In March 2014 the Company entered into a Consent Agreement with the DTCC to resolve alleged ITAR civil violations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among other things, the Consent Agreement required the Company to pay a $20&#160;million penalty, of which $10&#160;million was suspended and eligible for offset credit.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2016, the DTCC approved costs the Company incurred to implement compliance measures to fully offset the $10&#160;million suspended payment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Consent Agreement was closed in fiscal 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.19%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During fiscal 2015 the Company recognized a $15.7 million gain in other income and a $2.4 million reduction in interest expense upon the lapse of a statutory period related to a liability for a non-income tax position of an acquired company.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Company incurred a $2.9 million loss in other income on foreign currency exchange resulting from the funding of the acquisition of Esterline Advanced Displays.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.19%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In fiscal 2016 the Company received a $5&#160;million insurance recovery due to an energetic incident at one of our countermeasure operations, which occurred in the third quarter of fiscal 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company received a $7.8 million insurance recovery from this incident in fiscal 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Approximately 586 U.S.-based employees or 12% of total U.S.-based employees were represented by various labor unions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#8217;s non-U.S. operations are subject to union and national trade union agreements and to local regulations governing employment.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE&#160;13:&#160;&#160;<font style="font-weight:bold;">Employee Stock Plans</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has three share-based compensation plans, which are described below.&nbsp;&nbsp;The compensation cost that has been charged against income for those plans for fiscal 2017, 2016, and 2015 was $9.8&#160;million, $13.5&#160;million, and $10.8&#160;million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The total income tax benefit recognized in the income statement for the share-based compensation arrangement for fiscal 2017, 2016, and 2015 was $2.3&#160;million, $3.6&#160;million, and $2.7&#160;million, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employee Stock Purchase Plan</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company offers an employee stock purchase plan to its employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plan qualifies as a noncompensatory employee stock purchase plan under Section&#160;423 of the Internal Revenue Code.&nbsp;&nbsp;Employees are eligible to participate through payroll deductions subject to certain limitations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The plan has a safe harbor design where shares are purchased by participants at 95% of the fair market value on the purchase date and, therefore, compensation cost is not recorded.&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2017, employees purchased 18,183 shares at a fair market value price of $94.16 per share.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of September&#160;29, 2017, deductions aggregating $0.5&#160;million were accrued for the purchase of shares on December&#160;15, 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employee Share-Save Scheme</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company offers shares under its employee share-save scheme for U.K. employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;This plan allows participants the option to purchase shares at 95% of the market price of the stock as of the beginning of the offering period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The term of these options is three years.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the end of fiscal 2017, the Company had reserved 136,770 shares for issuance under its employee share-save scheme for U.K. employees, leaving a balance of 450,400 shares available for issuance in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;The share-save scheme is not a &#8220;safe-harbor&#8221; design, and, therefore, compensation cost is recognized on this plan. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the employee share-save scheme, option exercise prices are equal to the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company granted 11,338, 70,673 and 25,984 options in fiscal 2017, 2016, and 2015, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The weighted-average grant date fair value of options granted in fiscal 2017 was $24.61 per share.&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2017, 1,764 options were exercised at a weighted average exercise price of $69.12.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">71</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU70"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of the awards under the employee share-save scheme was estimated using a Black-Scholes pricing model which uses the</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> assumptions noted in the following table.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risk-free rate for the contractual life of the option is based on the U.S. Treasury zero coupon issues in effect the time of grant.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Equity Incentive Plan</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company also provides an equity incentive plan for officers and key employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the end of fiscal 2017, the Company had 3,617,032 shares reserved for issuance to officers and key employees, of which 2,455,036 shares were available to be granted in the future.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock Options</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Board of Directors authorized the Compensation Committee to administer awards granted under the Company&#8217;s 2013 Equity Incentive Plan and to establish the terms of such awards.&nbsp;&nbsp;Awards under the equity incentive plan may be granted to eligible employees of the Company over the 10-year period ending March&#160;5, 2023.&nbsp;&nbsp;Options granted generally become exercisable ratably over a period of four years following the date of grant and expire on the tenth anniversary of the grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;Option exercise prices are equal to the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;The weighted-average grant date fair value of the options granted in fiscal 2017 and 2016 was $32.72 per share and $35.69 per share, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of each option granted by the Company was estimated using a Black-Scholes pricing model which uses the assumptions noted in the following table.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company uses historical data to estimate volatility of the Company&#8217;s common stock and option exercise and employee termination assumptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The range of the expected term reflects the results from certain groups of employees exhibiting different behavior.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risk-free rate for the periods within the contractual life of the grant is based upon the U.S. Treasury zero coupon issues in effect at the time of the grant.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company granted 37,100 and 37,000 restricted stock units (RSUs) during fiscal 2017 and 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of each RSU granted by the Company is equal to the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;RSUs granted generally have a three-year cliff vesting schedule.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On June&#160;19,&#160;2014, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved a $200&#160;million share repurchase program.&nbsp;&nbsp;In March 2015, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved an additional $200&#160;million for the share repurchase program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the program, the Company is authorized to repurchase up to $400&#160;million of outstanding shares of common stock from time to time, depending on market conditions, share price and other factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;Repurchases may be made in the open market or through private transactions, in accordance with SEC requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company may enter into a Rule 10(b)5-1 plan designed to facilitate the repurchase of all or a portion of the repurchase amount.&nbsp;&nbsp;The program does not require the Company to acquire a specific number of shares.&nbsp;&nbsp;Common stock repurchased can be reissued, and accordingly, the Company accounts for repurchased stock under the cost method of accounting.&nbsp;&nbsp;There were no shares repurchased in fiscal 2017.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE&#160;15:&#160;&#160;<font style="font-weight:bold;">Acquisitions</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January&#160;31, 2015, the Company acquired the defense, aerospace and training display business, or Esterline Advanced Displays (EAD), of Belgium-based Barco N.V. (Barco) for &#8364;150&#160;million, or approximately $171&#160;million, in cash before a working capital adjustment of approximately $15&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Acquisition related costs of $3.4&#160;million were recognized as selling, general and administrative expense in fiscal 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The EAD acquisition contributed $151.6 million, $155.7&#160;million and $82.5&#160;million in sales and $7.8 million and $2.6&#160;million in operating earnings in fiscal 2017 and 2016, respectively and a $16.0&#160;million in operating losses in fiscal 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company financed the acquisition primarily using international cash reserves, with the balance funded by borrowings under its existing credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;The EAD business develops and manufactures visualization solutions for a variety of demanding defense and commercial aerospace applications and is included in our Avionics &amp; Controls segment.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE&#160;16:&#160;&#160;<font style="font-weight:bold;">Restructuring</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December&#160;5, 2013, the Company announced the acceleration of its plans to consolidate certain facilities and create cost efficiencies through shared services in sales, general and administrative and support functions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Restructuring expense totaled $8.7&#160;million in fiscal 2016 and $11.7&#160;million in fiscal 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The costs are mainly for exit and relocation of facilities, losses on the write off of certain property, plant and equipment, and severance.&nbsp;&nbsp;There were no restructuring expenses in fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE&#160;17:&#160;&#160;<font style="font-weight:bold;">Discontinued Operations</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s Board of Directors previously approved the plan to sell certain non-core business units including Eclipse Electronic Systems, Inc. (Eclipse), a manufacturer of embedded communication intercept receivers for signal intelligence applications; Wallop Defence Systems, Ltd. (Wallop), a manufacturer of flare countermeasure devices; Pacific Aerospace and Electronics Inc. (PA&amp;E), a manufacturer of hermetically sealed electrical connectors; a small distribution business; and a small manufacturing business. These businesses were not separate reporting units as defined under U.S. GAAP, and there was no indicator of impairment requiring an impairment test of their corresponding reporting units&#8217; goodwill or these businesses&#8217; long-lived assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon the estimated fair values, the Company incurred an estimated after-tax loss of $2.9&#160;million, $8.4&#160;million and $30.8&#160;million in fiscal 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively, on the assets held for sale in discontinued operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Principle assumptions used in measuring the estimated after-tax loss included estimated selling price of the discontinued business, discount rates, industry growth rates, and pricing of comparable transactions in the market.&nbsp;&nbsp;The additional losses on the assets were due to either the finalization of the selling prices of the assets disposed or to update the estimated fair values of the assets which continued to be held for sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;The estimated fair values were impacted by current market conditions for the sale transactions based mainly upon the status of negotiations with the potential buyers. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March 28, 2017, the Company sold a small manufacturing business for $0.6&#160;million and a note receivable of $2.4&#160;million, resulting in a gain on sale of the business of $0.8&#160;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The note receivable is due March 28, 2021, with an interest rate of 2.05%.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On May&#160;4, 2016, the Company sold certain assets of Wallop for 2.5&#160;million British pounds and deferred compensation up to a maximum payment of 9&#160;million British pounds.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the definitive purchase and sale agreement for the sale of these assets, the Company provided standard representations and warranties as well as indemnification to the buyer of the Wallop operation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is obligated to indemnify the buyer for certain losses of up to 5.0 million British pounds, if, among other things, the Company breaches the representations and warranties.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to September 29, 2017, the Company received notification of a claim from the buyer of the Wallop operation alleging breaches of representations and warranties primarily associated with defective products and late product deliveries.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although a loss is possible, the amount of any loss related to this claim cannot be estimated at this time.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not expect the possible loss to have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s financial position.&nbsp;&nbsp;The deferred compensation is payable based upon receipt of acceptable orders during a three-year period ending May&#160;3, 2019, and is equal to the amount of the acceptable order times a specified percentage ranging from 26.5% to 31%.&nbsp;&nbsp;The earn-out payment is estimated to be 5.6&#160;million British pounds at September&#160;29, 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On June&#160;5, 2015, the Company sold Eclipse for $7.9&#160;million and retained ownership of the land, building and building improvements, which are held for sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, on July&#160;20, 2015, the Company sold PA&amp;E for $22.3&#160;million.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company recorded an expense related to environmental remediation at a previously sold business for which the Company provided indemnification of $0.9&#160;million in fiscal 2017, $0.8&#160;million in fiscal 2016, and $2.1&#160;million in fiscal 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The liability for this environmental obligation was $0.1&#160;million and $0.8&#160;million at September&#160;29, 2017, and September&#160;30, 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Remediation costs paid in fiscal 2017, 2016, and 2015 were $1.6&#160;million, $1.5&#160;million and $2.0&#160;million, respectively.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">75</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE&#160;18:&#160;&#160;<font style="font-weight:bold;">Business Segment Information</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s businesses are organized and managed in three reporting segments:&nbsp;&nbsp;Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls, Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems and Advanced Materials.&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating segments within each reporting segment are aggregated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Operations within the Avionics&#160;&amp; Controls segment focus on integrated cockpit systems, technology interface systems for commercial and military aircraft, and similar devices for land- and sea-based military vehicles, visualization solutions for defense and commercial applications, secure communication systems, military audio and data products, specialized medical equipment and other industrial applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sensors&#160;&amp; Systems includes operations that produce high-precision temperature and pressure sensors, electrical power switching, electrical interconnection systems, and other related systems principally for aerospace and defense customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Advanced Materials segment focuses on thermally engineered components for critical aerospace applications, high-performance elastomer products used in a wide range of commercial aerospace and military applications, and combustible ordnance and warfare countermeasure devices.&nbsp;&nbsp;All segments include sales to domestic, international, defense and commercial customers.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Geographic sales information is based on product origin.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company evaluates these segments based on segment profits prior to net interest, other income/expense, corporate expenses and federal/foreign income taxes.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:1.78%;text-indent:-1.78%;font-size:5pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><br /></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">83</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU79"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Board of Directors and Shareholders</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Esterline Technologies Corporation<font style="font-weight:bold;"> </font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Esterline Technologies Corporation as of September 29, 2017 and September 30, 2016, and the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income (loss), cash flows, shareholders' equity, and noncontrolling interests for the twelve months ended September 29, 2017 and September 30, 2016, and the eleven months ended October 2, 2015. These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company's management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audits.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In our opinion, the financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated financial position of Esterline Technologies Corporation at September 29, 2017 and September 30, 2016, and the consolidated results of its operations and its cash flows for the twelve months ended September 29, 2017 and September 30, 2016, and the eleven months ended October 2, 2015, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. <font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), Esterline Technologies Corporation's internal control over financial reporting as of September 29, 2017, based on criteria established in Internal Control-Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) and our report dated November 21, 2017 expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">November 21, 2017</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU80"></a><font style="font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Report of Independent </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Registered Public Accounting Firm</font></p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Board of Directors and Shareholders </p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Esterline Technologies Corporation<font style="font-weight:bold;"> </font></p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have audited Esterline Technologies Corporation&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of September 29, 2017, based on criteria established in Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (the COSO criteria). Esterline Technologies Corporation&#8217;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting included in the accompanying Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit. <font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font></p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of the company&#8217;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In our opinion, Esterline Technologies Corporation maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of September 29, 2017, based on<font style="font-weight:bold;"> </font>the COSO criteria<font style="font-weight:bold;">.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the accompanying consolidated balances sheets of Esterline Technologies Corporation as of September 29, 2017 and September 30, 2016, and the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income (loss), cash flows, shareholders&#8217; equity, and noncontrolling interests for the twelve months ended September 29, 2017 and September 30, 2016, and the eleven months ended October 2, 2015 of Esterline Technologies Corporation and our report dated November 21, 2017 expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.<font style="margin-left:36pt;"></font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">November 21, 2017</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU81"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Item&#160;9.&#160;&#160;Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:8pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Item&#160;9A.&#160;&#160;Controls and Procedures</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our principal executive and financial officers evaluated our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules&#160;13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act) as of September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon that evaluation, they concluded as of September&#160;29, 2017, that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective to ensure that information we are required to disclose in the reports that we file under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within time periods specified in Securities and Exchange Commission rules and forms.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, our principal executive and financial officers concluded as of September&#160;29, 2017, that our disclosure controls and procedures are also effective to ensure that information required to be disclosed in reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our chief executive officer and chief financial officer, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rules&#160;13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our internal control system over financial reporting is designed by, or under the supervision of, our chief executive officer and chief financial officer, and is effected by our Board of Directors, management and other personnel to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that:</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.2%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(i)<font style="margin-left:54pt;">pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the assets of the company;</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.2%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(ii)<font style="margin-left:54pt;">provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessar</font>y to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and that transactions are made only in accordance with the authorization of our management and directors; and</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.2%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(iii)<font style="margin-left:54pt;">provide reasonable assuranc</font>e regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized transactions that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Because of inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, even those systems determined to be effective can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation and presentation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in condition, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management assessed the effectiveness of Esterline&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of September&#160;29, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;In making this assessment, our management used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in Internal Control-Integrated Framework (2013 framework).&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on management&#8217;s assessment and those criteria, our management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of September&#160;29, 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">86</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU82"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our independent registered public accounting firm, Ernst&#160;&amp;</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> Young LLP, has issued an audit report on the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;This report appears on page </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">85</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</font></p>
